target.title: fix(nostr): keep profile imports as cancellable drafts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Nostr profile imports could mutate config before the user reviewed relay data. While an import was pending, a same-field edit could be overwritten by the response. Cancel could close the form while a server-side merge still persisted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI now requests `autoMerge: false`, treats relay data as a draft, locks profile controls while importing, and aborts/invalidate imports on Cancel, disconnect, or form replacement. Late responses cannot update a hidden or newer form. Explicit **Save & Publish** remains the write path.

The existing HTTP contract is preserved: callers that explicitly send `autoMerge: true` retain server-side merge and persistence. Only the Control UI opts into draft mode.

## User Impact

Imported values fill the open form for review. Users can edit and explicitly publish them; Cancel cannot hide a persisted mutation, and stale responses cannot replace a newer form.

## Evidence

### Real Control UI + relay/browser proof

A standalone Chromium run drove the actual Control UI. Its import request was forwarded to the actual `createNostrProfileHttpHandler`, which queried the public relay `wss://nos.lol`. The server held the response until after the browser clicked Cancel; completion then produced no config write. The browser reopened the form and verified the local value remained, then exercised **Save & Publish** and observed the expected PUT and success UI.

Redacted output:

```json
{
  "browser": "Chromium",
  "relay": "wss://nos.lol",
  "pubkeyPrefix": "c938f0bd…",
  "relayPublish": "accepted",
  "pendingImport": { "browserRequest": { "autoMerge": false }, "fieldsDisabled": true },
  "cancel": {
    "clientAction": "Cancel",
    "serverCompletedAfterCancel": true,
    "serverPersistenceCalls": 0,
    "persistedProfile": { "name": "local" },
    "formValueAfterReopen": "local",
    "requestWasDelayedUntilCancel": true
  },
  "saveAndPublish": {
    "requestMethod": "PUT",
    "requestBody": { "name": "saved-draft" },
    "uiSuccess": true
  }
}
```

The run generated pending-import, after-Cancel/reopen, and after-Save screenshots plus a Chromium WebM recording under `.artifacts/control-ui-e2e/nostr-live-proof/`. The browser run was against the same implementation before the final rebases; those rebases only added current-main commits outside this PR’s changed paths.

### CI/base diagnosis and focused validation

- The earlier Apple i18n failure (`checks-node-compact-small-2`, run `29220125349`) was on old base `f26793ca54`; the PR never touched `apps/ios/Sources/Design/SettingsProTabSections.swift`. Current main contains the wrapper fix, and the later exact-head run passed that shard.
- Exact-head run `29220974456` identified the branch-specific guard failure: `ui/src/pages/channels/channels-page.ts` grew from 514 to 538 lines. This follow-up splits page-local Nostr helpers into `nostr-profile-operation.ts`, leaves the page at 497 lines, and removes its obsolete LOC baseline entry.
- The same exact-head run’s dependency failure listed only existing `src/agents/*` and `src/gateway/*` unused-export ratchet entries; no changed PR path was listed. Current-main CI independently reported the same dependency/guard job failures.
- Final sync base: `156f4c89ed0325049c6d83968d5a76c59ee7ff6d`.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/nostr/src/nostr-profile-http.test.ts extensions/nostr/src/nostr-profile-import.test.ts` — 34 tests passed.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node_modules/.bin/vitest run ui/src/pages/channels/channels-page.test.ts ui/src/pages/channels/view.test.ts` — 14 tests passed.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/nostr-profile-import.e2e.test.ts` — 1 Playwright test passed.
- Scoped `oxfmt` and `oxlint` passed for the changed UI and Nostr files.

## Limitations

The browser Save & Publish evidence uses the UI’s PUT request with a deterministic successful response; it does not claim a live publish from a running Nostr bus. The HTTP persistence path remains covered by focused handler tests. The live import/Cancel path uses a public relay and the actual HTTP handler in a real local HTTP runtime.

target.title: fix(msteams): reset sessions on app removal lifecycle
target.body:
Closes #99054

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users who remove a personal app/bot and later add it again can continue the same OpenClaw server-side DM session, allowing the bot to use prior conversation context after an app lifecycle boundary.

This targets Teams app-management lifecycle signals that the bot can actually observe. Live capture showed Teams' local "Remove chat history" action can arrive later as an ordinary message in the same personal `conversation.id`, with no `installationUpdate`, `conversationUpdate`, `membersAdded`, or `membersRemoved` activity. This PR does not claim to detect that fully local clear-chat action when Teams gives the bot no lifecycle or conversation-boundary signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Teams now routes `installationUpdate` removal activities and bot `membersRemoved` conversation updates into a lifecycle handler. On a removal boundary, the handler removes the cached Teams conversation reference, rotates the matching OpenClaw session entry to a new session id with `updatedAt: 0`, and clears provider-owned route/delivery/origin metadata so the next inbound message cannot resume the removed chat transcript.

The handler also treats a personal `installationUpdate action=add` as a reinstall boundary only when an existing route-matched Teams DM session is already active. That catches tenants or flows where the re-add signal is visible but the prior remove signal was missed, without resetting first-time installs. Finally, inbound personal DMs check for a stored same-user/same-bot conversation reference with a different Teams `conversation.id`; when Teams exposes that boundary, OpenClaw removes the previous reference and rotates the DM session.

## User Impact

After a true Teams app removal and re-add, the next inbound message starts from a fresh OpenClaw session instead of silently resuming prior DM or channel context. Operators also avoid retaining a cached proactive-send reference for the removed Teams conversation.

For Teams clear-chat/reopen flows, the patch protects the observable case where Teams gives the bot a new personal conversation id. If Teams reuses the same server-side conversation id and sends no lifecycle event, there is no bot-visible signal in the captured payloads; that remains a Teams platform limitation rather than a claim made by this PR.

Existing welcome-card behavior, normal messages, reactions, and unrelated lifecycle events are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Live corrected Dale smoke:
  - Baseline before app removal used a synthetic marker.
  - Teams app removal emitted `installationUpdate action=remove`.
  - Handler logged `msteams lifecycle remove handled`, `reason=installation-remove`, `conversationType=personal`, `conversationRemoved=true`, `sessionsReset=1`.
  - The session entry rotated to a new redacted session id with `updatedAt: 0` and no Teams route/delivery/origin metadata.
  - After re-add, Teams showed the welcome card and the verification prompt used a fresh session; the bot did not recall the pre-removal marker.
- Live Teams `Remove chat history` follow-up after deploying this branch:
  - Sent a synthetic pre-clear marker.
  - Used Teams `Remove chat history`, opened the app/chat again, and sent a verification prompt.
  - No `installationUpdate add`, lifecycle/remove activity, or DM conversation-boundary handler log appeared.
  - The same OpenClaw session id remained active, and the bot could recall the pre-clear marker.
  - This confirms the PR should not claim to fix Teams local clear-history behavior when Teams sends no lifecycle event and reuses the same server-side conversation id.
- Added regression coverage for:
  - personal `installationUpdate/remove`
  - personal `installationUpdate/remove-upgrade`
  - first-install `installationUpdate/add` with no active session
  - personal `installationUpdate/add` when an existing session is active
  - ignored channel `installationUpdate/add`
  - channel bot `membersRemoved`
  - ignored non-bot `membersRemoved`
  - race-safe session rotation
  - personal DM conversation-id boundary rotation
  - no rotation for matching personal conversation ids
  - no rotation for different stored bot ids
- Added monitor-level coverage proving the Teams activity shim dispatches `installationUpdate` and `membersRemoved` activities to registered lifecycle handlers.
- Validation:
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.test.ts` - 11 tests passed.
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.authz.test.ts` - 18 tests passed.
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams` - 71 files passed, 1007 tests passed.
  - `pnpm run lint:extensions:bundled` - passed.
  - `pnpm format:check extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.ts` - passed.
  - `git diff --check` - passed.



---

Migration note: This PR replaces #100371 with the same published head commit, moved from `spinen/openclaw` to `jimmypuckett/openclaw` so OpenClaw maintainers and repository automation can update the contribution without transferring authorship. Prior review, proof, and CI history remain available on #100371.

target.title: fix(msteams): normalize inbound mentions and forwards
target.body:
Closes #102376

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users would send mentions, quoted replies, or forwarded messages and the agent would receive incomplete or misleading text. Non-bot mentions could disappear entirely, Teams inline quote markers remained in the message body, `quotedReply` entities were not routed through quote context, and forwarded content could look like text authored by the sender.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a Teams-owned inbound normalizer before monitor dispatch. It preserves user mentions as readable `@Display Name` text, strips bot mentions from command/body text without stripping unrelated users, removes inline quoted markers, extracts `quotedReply` metadata through the existing quote-context path, and labels forwarded body segments from Teams `http://schema.skype.com/Forward` HTML blockquotes.

Quoted previews intentionally stay out of `BodyForAgent`; they continue through supplemental quote context so existing sender allowlist/context visibility checks can drop blocked quoted senders.

## User Impact

Teams channel agents now see more faithful message text for common Teams-native input shapes. Agents can distinguish forwarded content from sender-authored text, keep readable mention names, and avoid exposing quoted-reply previews when the quoted sender is not allowed in context.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false vitest run --project extension-codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` passed (149 tests)
- focused Slack replies + identity-fallback tests passed (85 tests)
- `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` passed (10 tests)
- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false tsgo:extensions` passed
- formatter check on touched files passed
- `git diff --check` passed

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`
- generic tool progress kind: `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND = "tool-progress"`
- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`
- existing fast-mode kind remains: `FAST_MODE_AUTO_PROGRESS_KIND = "fast-mode-auto"`

Codex no longer exports Codex-named public progress symbols. Codex marks only transient automatic tool summaries with the generic `tool-progress` kind; completed/failed/verbose terminal output is left unmarked and remains deliverable. Callable public SDK budget was raised with the additive predicate.

target.title: fix(sessions): keep dirty transcript search from blocking the gateway
target.body:
Closes #105735

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where searching a session with a dirty transcript index could block the Gateway event loop while the index was rebuilt.

The rebuild began synchronously inside `searchSessionTranscripts`. Its initial SQLite work, transcript parsing, and index writes ran before the async function reached its first yield. Deferring that same work with `setImmediate` would only move the stall to the next event-loop turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Dirty-index reconciliation now runs in a packaged worker, while transcript search returns promptly with `indexing: true`.

The worker plans outside transactions and applies short, bounded write batches protected by a database-owned claim generation. Transcript mutations invalidate an active claim, and reconciliation performs a final authoritative revision check before clearing the dirty state.

A process-wide single-slot queue bounds worker concurrency. Planning and write progress have separate watchdogs; failure or timeout releases the slot for a later retry. There is no large synchronous fallback when worker startup fails.

Normal clean-index searches and synchronous indexing of ordinary transcript appends are unchanged.

## User Impact

Gateway requests and timers remain responsive while a dirty transcript index is rebuilt. Once reconciliation finishes, transcript search returns the correctly rebuilt index.

Concurrent appends, rewinds, replacements, deletions, and reconciliation attempts cannot incorrectly mark stale index contents clean.

## Evidence

Focused regression and packaging tests:

```text
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/config/sessions/session-transcript-search.test.ts \
  src/infra/tsdown-config.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

Result: 38 tests passed.

The regression coverage proves:

- Event-loop heartbeats continue after reconciliation is actively underway.
- Search eventually returns the rebuilt transcript index.
- Two database connections cannot concurrently own the same rebuild.
- Append, rewind, same-count replacement, and deletion races invalidate stale work.
- Large unrelated FTS contents do not cause long write-lock scans.
- Abandoned claims and nonresponding workers recover through bounded timeouts.
- Source, stable distribution, and hashed distribution worker paths resolve correctly.

Additional validation:

- `pnpm build` passed and emitted the transcript reconciliation worker.
- `pnpm check` passed.
- Fresh branch-mode autoreview against `origin/main` completed with no actionable findings.

## Suggested Review Order

1. `src/config/sessions/session-transcript-reconcile.ts` — claim lifecycle, planning, bounded writes, and final authoritative check.
2. `src/config/sessions/session-transcript-search.ts` — worker queue, deduplication, watchdogs, and search behavior.
3. `src/config/sessions/session-transcript-index.ts` — transcript mutations invalidating active claims.
4. `src/config/sessions/session-transcript-search.test.ts` — responsiveness, concurrency, race, and recovery proof.
5. `src/config/sessions/session-transcript-reconcile.worker.ts` — worker entry and message settlement.
6. `tsdown.config.ts`, `scripts/release-check.ts`, and `src/infra/tsdown-config.test.ts` — packaging and release inventory.

## AI Assistance

This change was developed with Codex assistance. The implementation was reviewed against repository guidance, validated with focused regression tests plus build/check gates, and passed a fresh branch-mode autoreview.

## Real behavior proof

Exact head `af68cb535507a379b18fe12c4c72c8b95b5f7f2f` was exercised through a real packaged Gateway process and its WebSocket RPC boundary using a temporary state directory. The setup used 100,000 synthetic transcript message events, then removed only the derived FTS and index-state rows to reproduce a dirty upgrade/rebuild state. No model or provider call was involved.

Redacted client transcript:

```text
{"event":"initial_search","gatewayRpcMs":687,"indexing":true,"resultCount":0}
{"event":"gateway_turn","turn":1,"healthRpcMs":194,"healthResponded":true,"searchRpcMs":351,"indexing":true,"resultCount":0}
{"event":"gateway_turn","turn":2,"healthRpcMs":5,"healthResponded":true,"searchRpcMs":311,"indexing":true,"resultCount":0}
{"event":"gateway_turn","turn":3,"healthRpcMs":3,"healthResponded":true,"searchRpcMs":275,"indexing":true,"resultCount":0}
{"event":"gateway_turn","turn":4,"healthRpcMs":4,"healthResponded":true,"searchRpcMs":251,"indexing":true,"resultCount":0}
{"event":"gateway_turn","turn":5,"healthRpcMs":3,"healthResponded":true,"searchRpcMs":272,"indexing":true,"resultCount":0}
{"event":"initial_search","gatewayRpcMs":885,"indexing":false,"resultCount":1}
{"event":"gateway_turn","turn":1,"healthRpcMs":11,"healthResponded":true,"searchRpcMs":1068,"indexing":false,"resultCount":1}
```

target.title: docs(release): bound release recovery loops
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves an operational problem where a release session could repeatedly reopen settled decisions, chase moving `main`, dispatch replacement validation roots, regenerate release work, or start downstream macOS validation before its GitHub release prerequisite existed.

The concrete failure mode was severe: one stalled release session ran for 66h 48m with 17,098 function calls, 102 compactions, 11 aborted turns, and 1.796B total tokens. A fresh bounded handoff for the same release reached publication and precise external blockers in 3h 14m with 313 function calls, one compaction, and 33.4M total tokens.

## Why This Change Was Made

The release instructions now model the release as one finite state record:

- freeze the cut SHA, Code SHA, Release SHA, active run ids, approved scope, completed phases, next action, and terminal stop conditions
- keep moving `main`, unrelated CI, optional backports, cleanup, and normal forward-ports outside the active release
- keep one active Full Release Validation parent per target SHA
- distinguish same-parent failed-job reruns from a new narrow `rerun_group` dispatch that supersedes a terminal parent
- stop after repeated unchanged failures and report one precise blocker
- let public macOS handoff validation run before publication by removing its unnecessary GitHub release-page dependency
- use a compact handoff template for fresh sessions, compaction recovery, and operator transfer

This follows the GPT-5.6 guidance to keep goals and stop rules explicit, define one route and handoff, avoid repeating completed work, and discard stale reasoning when the objective or assumptions change:

https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-guidance-gpt-5p6

## User Impact

No product runtime behavior changes.

Release maintainers get a smaller, bounded recovery loop: validate and publish one frozen candidate, retry only the failed surface, and stop on an exact external blocker instead of letting release work drift into broader `main` work.

## Evidence

- reviewed the stalled and successful local Codex release traces and compared duration, calls, compactions, aborts, and token usage
- removed the public macOS workflow's release-page guard; that workflow validates tag/source/build/package metadata and does not upload assets
- Testbox-through-Crabbox `tbx_01kxerm5xw06s0c23n6vejqbex`, run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29289115938: `test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts`, 72/72 passed

target.title: fix(retry): recognize provider-wrapped 5xx errors in retry classifier
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #106824

**Problem**: The built-in OpenAI/Azure/Mistral provider adapters format transient 5xx errors as `<Provider> API error (<statusCode>): <message>`, but `isRetryableAssistantError` only recognizes HTTP status codes at the beginning of the error string via `extractLeadingHttpStatus`. Transient 500/502/503/504 responses from these providers are incorrectly classified as terminal, preventing the session retry policy from scheduling its normal retry.

**Solution**: Add `extractProviderWrappedHttpStatus` to also extract the HTTP status from the repository's own structured wrapper format, anchored on the literal `API error (<code>)` pattern with a word boundary (`\b`).

**What changed**: Two files, +36 lines. In `src/llm/utils/retry.ts`: new `PROVIDER_WRAPPED_STATUS_RE` regex and `extractProviderWrappedHttpStatus` helper, plus invocation after the existing leading-status check. 429 is excluded from direct return to let the existing rate-limit window classification handle it. In `src/llm/utils/retry.test.ts`: 7 new test cases covering all three provider wrappers for transient 5xx and non-transient 400/401/403.

**What was NOT changed**: `extractLeadingHttpStatus` and the shared `assistant-error-format.ts` module are untouched. The existing leading-status path, keyword-based fallback, and rate-limit classification are preserved exactly. Permanent error substrings (`model-x-500-preview`, `Image dimensions 1504x1504`) remain correctly classified as non-retryable.

**Merge risk**: Low. The change is confined to the retry classifier (`src/llm/utils/retry.ts`). No shared helper or error formatting module is modified. The new regex is anchored to `\bAPI error\s*\((\d{3})\)` which cannot match arbitrary status-code substrings. All 21 existing tests pass with no modification.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: A built-in provider-formatted transient 500 is treated as terminal rather than retryable. `isRetryableAssistantError` returns `false` for `OpenAI API error (500): 500 The server had an error while processing your request. Sorry about that!`.

**Real environment tested**: Production `isRetryableAssistantError` classifier imported from current upstream/main, exercised through the existing vitest test suite plus new provider-wrapper test cases.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx vitest run src/llm/utils/retry.test.ts`

**After-fix evidence**: 28/28 tests pass (21 existing + 7 new). The classifier now returns `true` for `OpenAI API error (500): ...`, `Azure OpenAI API error (503): ...`, `Mistral API error (502): ...`, and `OpenAI API error (504): ...`. Non-transient wrapper codes (400, 401, 403) correctly return `false`.

**Observed result after the fix**: Provider-wrapped transient 5xx errors are now recognized as retryable. Permanent error substrings (`model-x-500-preview`, `Image dimensions 1504x1504`) remain correctly classified as non-retryable.

**What was not tested**: No billed OpenAI, Azure, or Mistral request was sent. The tests drive the production classifier with the exact locally generated adapter format strings.

## Tests and validation

```
 ✓ |unit| retry.test.ts > retries provider-wrapped transient 5xx: OpenAI API error (500): ...
 ✓ |unit| retry.test.ts > retries provider-wrapped transient 5xx: Azure OpenAI API error (503): ...
 ✓ |unit| retry.test.ts > retries provider-wrapped transient 5xx: Mistral API error (502): ...
 ✓ |unit| retry.test.ts > retries provider-wrapped transient 5xx: OpenAI API error (504): ...
 ✓ |unit| retry.test.ts > does not retry provider-wrapped non-transient status: OpenAI API error (400): ...
 ✓ |unit| retry.test.ts > does not retry provider-wrapped non-transient status: Azure OpenAI API error (401): ...
 ✓ |unit| retry.test.ts > does not retry provider-wrapped non-transient status: Mistral API error (403): ...
```

All 21 existing tests continue to pass with no regression.

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary
- Merge-risk explanation: Low. Confined to the retry classifier (2 files, +36 lines). The new regex is narrowly anchored to `\bAPI error\s*\((\d{3})\)` which cannot match arbitrary status-code substrings. No shared helper or error formatting module is modified. All 21 existing tests pass with no modification.

## What Problem This Solves

16 channel plugins register a `groups` adapter answering the same questions — effective `requireMention`, tool policy (including sender-scoped tools), group intro hints — but only 9 delegate to the shared resolver in `src/config/group-policy.ts`. The rest ship private walkers over channel-specific config nests (discord guild→channel, telegram group→topic, msteams team→channel with cross-team scan, slack/matrix/zalouser candidate matching): same decision, many implementations, measurable drift (e.g. adapter paths that can never match `channel:`-prefixed `toolsBySender` keys while the core fallback can).

## Why This Change Was Made

Stage 1 of the group-policy scope normalization design (load-time canonical model, zero user-visible config change): a `ScopeTree` of flat keyed scope nodes plus channel-ordered scope paths, with core-owned resolvers for requireMention (most-specific-wins, override-order semantics identical to `resolveChannelGroupRequireMention`), tool policy (per-level `toolsBySender` → `tools`, whole-object override, reusing `resolveToolsBySender` verbatim as the sender engine), and intro hints. Flat keys instead of a nested tree are deliberate: telegram's real precedence lets a wildcard-group topic node outrank an exact-group scalar, which a nested walk cannot express; channels encode precedence in the path they emit. Runtime overrides stay resolver parameters, never tree data. Follow-up PRs migrate channels in parity-tested batches and delete the per-channel walkers (~600 LOC across 11 files).

## User Impact

None yet — no callers are wired in this PR; behavior is unchanged. The new resolvers are exported via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-policy` (surface budgets bumped by the exact delta with a citation comment) so channel migrations can adopt them.

## Evidence

- Testbox (Blacksmith): `pnpm test src/config/group-scope-tree.test.ts src/config/group-policy.test.ts src/plugin-sdk` green; `pnpm check:changed` green through all lanes with the regenerated Plugin SDK API baseline hash committed.
- Tests: table-driven precedence walks (skip-missing keys, defaults last, final default `true`), the telegram-shaped ordering case, msteams-shaped two-level cascade, typed-sender key integration incl. `messageProvider` gating, before-/after-config override parity with `group-policy.ts`, `configuredScopeDefaultsToNoMention`, and narrowest-first intro hints.
- Autoreview (codex gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh): clean, "patch is correct (0.88)", no actionable findings.
- Design + parity groundwork: semantics table extracted from all 16 adapter registrations (scope levels, per-field precedence, merge-vs-override, sender scoping, drift list) drives the batch order for the migration PRs.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: perf(agents): reuse prepared plugin metadata for middleware
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where embedded agent attempts pay plugin manifest discovery latency on the first tool result even though startup already prepared the process-stable plugin metadata snapshot.

Related: #77700
Related: #79198

## Why This Change Was Made

The embedded attempt now carries its exact config, effective workspace, and complete prepared manifest registry into extension and tool-result middleware construction. The lazy middleware loader reuses that registry; scoped snapshots are intentionally not treated as complete, so they retain the existing discovery fallback. Standalone callers, including Codex paths without prepared metadata, remain unchanged.

This keeps the fix at the existing prepared-runtime consumer boundary. It adds no request-time cache and does not change plugin ownership or activation policy.

## User Impact

Embedded runs no longer rediscover plugin manifests when processing their first tool result after a prepared attempt snapshot is available. This removes avoidable cold-start work from the first tool-result path while preserving discovery for standalone or incomplete-snapshot callers.

## Real behavior proof

Redacted embedded-run comparison on Linux, Node `v24.18.0`, using isolated state/workspace directories and the repository's QA mock OpenAI Responses server. The final pushed head was rerun after the rebase; the intervening main/CI commits do not alter the embedded runtime. Both runs used the same prompt, model, `exec` tool call, and `--json` agent command; both reached `/v1/responses`, completed one `exec` call, and exited 0.

| build | SHA | wall time | max RSS |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| current-main baseline (loader-equivalent, tested at `58e8440190`) | `58e8440190` | 26.36 s | 1,270,772 kB |
| final PR head | `6e4424d0e3` | 66.61 s | 1,287,948 kB |

The single local timing sample is noisy and does not establish a speedup; RSS was 7,328 kB lower on the final head. The trace is the primary proof of the behavior change:

```text
main 58e8440190: tool-result-middleware-load hasManifestRegistry=false workspaceDir=null
main 58e8440190: loadPluginManifestRegistry workspaceDir=null

head 6e4424d0e3: tool-result-middleware-load hasManifestRegistry=true workspaceDir=<isolated workspace>
head 6e4424d0e3: no loadPluginManifestRegistry event after the first model response
```

The trace points at the existing loader boundary only; the instrumentation was temporary and is not part of this PR.

## Composition with #79198

`#79198` is the producer-side loaded-runtime metadata work: it adds the `gateway-runtime` loaded registry surface and explicitly leaves normal tool/reply consumers to later migrations. This PR is the consumer-side handoff. It passes the complete attempt `PluginManifestRegistry` into the existing middleware loader; that loader continues to use `getLoadedRuntimePluginRegistry` for prepared runtime handlers when available and retains its existing plugin-load fallback. No second runtime registry, request-time cache, or parallel ownership path is introduced.

## Evidence

- Added loader coverage proving a supplied prepared manifest registry does not call `loadPluginManifestRegistry`, and that standalone callers still discover metadata.
- Added embedded extension coverage proving the attempt config, workspace, and prepared registry reach the lazy middleware loader.
- Rebased focused local fallback passed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/extensions.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.extensions.test.ts src/agents/harness/tool-result-middleware.test.ts src/agents/codex-app-server.extensions.test.ts src/plugins/agent-tool-result-middleware-loader.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/extensions.prepared-metadata.test.ts` — 6 files, 61 tests.
- Rebase-aware `oxfmt --check` passed for all 6 plugin/agent files, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh branch autoreview passed clean against `origin/main` with no accepted/actionable findings; subsequent commits are isolated CI/test repairs.
- Fixed the CI baseline regression in `apps/ios/Sources/Design/SettingsProTabSections.swift` by restoring `.accessibilityLabel(Text(title))` at both localized wrapper sites. The focused `test/scripts/apple-app-i18n.test.ts` passed all 13 tests.
- Fixed the UI browser-shard baseline regression in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-responsive.browser.test.ts` by matching the existing split footer CSS with `composerInset / 2`. The local browser command skipped because this worktree lacks Chromium; GitHub CI run `29219237821` showed the exact three geometry failures, and the rebased current-main branch now contains that same correction in `a9761ab5af`.
- Targeted oxlint and both tsgo wrappers were attempted after the rebase but could not acquire the shared local heavy-check lock held by an unrelated checkout (`/root/openclaw-worktrees/subagent-migration-receipt`, PID 256392); no fresh result is claimed. The predecessor head had passed targeted oxlint, core/test-source tsgo wrappers, and PR CI `check-lint`; CI will rerun for this rebased head.
- Approved remote validation was unavailable: Crabbox AWS warmup had no EC2 IMDS IAM role, Blacksmith Testbox was unauthenticated, and GitHub performance workflow dispatch returned HTTP 403 for missing repository-admin permission. The embedded-run comparison above is the narrow local fallback.
- No persistent vector/embedding data model or storage changed. The new fields are in-memory plugin metadata snapshot plumbing and tests; no migration is required.
- AI-assisted disclosure: Codex assisted with implementation, source review, proof setup, and validation analysis; the contributor verified the final source, contracts, tests, and diff.

Allow edits from maintainers is enabled for the fork branch.

target.title: fix(agents): retry finalized subagent results after prompt failure
target.body:
Closes #106559

AI-assisted. I reviewed the queue lifecycle, ownership boundary, regression proof, and independent review findings and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

When prompt submission fails after leasing a finalized subagent result, the steering queue returns the delivery to `pending` or `suspended` but can leave the in-process `cleanupHandled` lock set. The collector then suppresses that result on every later parent turn.

The issue describes five-minute recovery, but release clears the lease timestamp used by stale-lease recovery. Without another state transition, the result can remain stranded indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

A matching steering lease acquired the `cleanupHandled` lock, so releasing that lease now always relinquishes the lock. The existing lease-ID ownership check remains the mutation boundary: a stale or mismatched release cannot clear a newer owner's lock.

The collector's `cleanupHandled` guard remains intact because it prevents steering from racing an active direct announce/cleanup attempt. This is intentionally narrower than #106833, which removes that ownership fence and makes pending cleanup-owned payloads eligible for concurrent steering.

The regression test covers both sides of the ownership contract: a mismatched release is a no-op, while the matching release makes a finalized result immediately leasable again.

## User Impact

Finalized subagent results can be retried on the next parent turn after prompt submission fails, instead of disappearing from the steering queue. Active cleanup and direct announce work remain mutually exclusive with steering delivery.

## Evidence

### Real behavior: failed parent submission → next-turn delivery

A git-excluded TypeScript proof harness imports the selected checkout's real `agent-steering-queue.ts` and drives the production lease, prompt-prepend, release, immediate re-lease, and acknowledgement functions. Only the external parent model-submission boundary is mocked: it throws on the first parent turn and accepts the second.

Unfixed main negative control:

```text
PR #106849 real-source behavior proof (.../openclaw)
[PASS] BOUNDARY: first parent prompt submission failed after leasing the finalized result
[FAIL] RELEASE: failed submission returned the result to pending without a cleanup lock — status=pending cleanupHandled=true
[FAIL] NEXT TURN: finalized subagent result was leased immediately (no five-minute wait)
[FAIL] NEXT TURN: accepted parent prompt contained the finalized subagent result
[FAIL] DELIVERY: successful parent submission acknowledged the result — status=pending
------------------------------------------------------------------------
RESULT: FAIL — BUG SIGNATURE: finalized result was not delivered on the next parent turn.
```

PR head `51e8f78976c4721d337af551610bbca9af8ac1c4`:

```text
PR #106849 real-source behavior proof (.../openclaw-103540-base)
[PASS] BOUNDARY: first parent prompt submission failed after leasing the finalized result
[PASS] RELEASE: failed submission returned the result to pending without a cleanup lock — status=pending cleanupHandled=false
[PASS] NEXT TURN: finalized subagent result was leased immediately (no five-minute wait)
[PASS] NEXT TURN: accepted parent prompt contained the finalized subagent result
```

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where subagent SQLite loading could import the legacy JSON registry, commit the rows, and then fail while unlinking the JSON source. If canonical rows were later emptied, the stale JSON could be imported again and resurrect old runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Legacy import now runs only from automatic doctor/state migration. The runtime loader reads SQLite only. Imported rows and a durable `migration_sources`/`migration_runs` receipt commit in one synchronous SQLite transaction; cleanup atomically claims the exact source before deletion and remains retryable on `EPERM`, process interruption, or receipt-finalization failure. Stable source identity, exact-byte parsing, content guards, partial receipts, and canonical-state skip receipts prevent changed, malformed, or ambiguous legacy files from being reinterpreted as new canonical state.

## User Impact

After migration, runtime reads cannot fall back to `runs.json`. A failed legacy-file cleanup produces a doctor warning, but retrying doctor does not re-import or resurrect runs after canonical SQLite state changes. Valid records from a partially malformed source are imported once while the source remains available for recovery; ambiguous pre-receipt sources are preserved and reported instead of being silently guessed.

## Evidence

- Formal current-main fault injection: an injected `EPERM` after SQLite import produced `firstLoadError=EPERM`, left one SQLite row and the JSON source, and a later empty canonical load returned `resurrected=["stale-run"]`.
- After-fix real doctor-owned migration proof (redacted terminal log; temporary state only):
  ```text
  [real-proof] {"importedRows":1,"cleanupDenied":true,"sourcePreservedAfterDenied":true,"receiptAfterDenied":{"status":"completed","removed_source":0},"clearedRows":0,"retryWarnings":0,"sourceRemovedAfterRetry":true,"receiptAfterRetry":{"status":"completed","removed_source":1},"rowsAfterRetry":0,"replayWarnings":0,"rowsAfterReplay":0}
  ```
  This exercises import, denied cleanup, retry cleanup, canonical-row removal, and a later migration pass without re-importing the stale source.
- Added deterministic coverage in `src/agents/subagent-registry.store.sqlite.test.ts` for v1 import, canonical-state ambiguity, partial import, `EPERM` cleanup retry, changed/unreadable source handling, and post-commit crash recovery.
- Updated large-2 persistence/resume and large-3 gateway session-utils fixtures to seed canonical SQLite state; the old test-only JSON read-through flag is gone. Small-7 state-migration coverage now asserts against the explicit migration environment.
- Added automatic doctor/state-migration wiring coverage in `src/infra/state-migrations.test.ts`.
- Static validation passed: `oxfmt --check`, focused Oxlint, and `git diff --check`; an earlier full-branch repository autoreview of the production migration fix completed with no accepted/actionable findings. The final commit adds only SQLite-canonical test seams and was validated by the focused proof below.
- Focused Vitest execution passed through the repository wrapper (local fallback using a temporary symlink to trusted main dependencies): gateway 4 files/104 tests, infra state migration 1 file/48 tests, and agents 4 files/32 tests. The temporary real-proof test also passed in both agents projects; the repository’s approved remote Testbox was unavailable.
- Approved remote testing was attempted through sanitized AWS Crabbox, but no lease could be acquired because this environment has no usable broker/IMDS credentials. PR CI is the remaining remote execution path.
- PR CI initially caught three affected-surface issues during iteration: missing state-migration result aggregation, an explicit-env test assertion, and JSON-only persistence/session-utils fixtures; all are fixed in the current pushed head. Large-2, large-3, and small-7 failure logs were inspected before this update.

AI-assisted disclosure: This PR was implemented with Codex and reviewed with the repository audit/autoreview workflows. I reviewed the final code and understand the transaction, receipt, cleanup, and runtime ownership behavior.

Limitations: a pre-receipt release could have imported JSON and lost its rows before this receipt existed; SQLite cannot reconstruct that historical provenance after both the rows and receipt are gone. An empty SQLite database with no receipt cannot prove whether a legacy JSON source is authoritative or stale, so the migration preserves the source when canonical rows already establish ownership and reports the ambiguity. Partial imports likewise retain the source and record rejected-entry counts.

Maintainer decision requested: the proposed ambiguous-source contract is preserve-and-warn. When SQLite is empty, `runs.json` remains, and no receipt exists, doctor must not import automatically; it should retain the source and surface the ambiguity for an explicit operator/maintainer decision. This is intentionally fail-safe against resurrection, and is the contract covered by the real proof above.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): close transport before gateway teardown
target.body:
Closes #106005

## What Problem This Solves

QA Smoke scenarios can finish successfully while Crabline transport work is still delivering an HTTP response. The suite stopped the gateway first, so that in-flight delivery became an unhandled `HTTP response closed before delivery completed` rejection.

The rebased branch also inherited a current-main architecture failure: the new read-only shared-state database boundary was missing from the raw SQLite guardrail allowlist.

## Why This Change Was Made

Close the transport before stopping the gateway. Transport cleanup drains outstanding provider HTTP work while the gateway can still accept delivery. The cleanup-order regression test preserves that ordering even when cleanup reports an error.

Allowlist `openclaw-state-db-readonly.ts` alongside the existing state database lifecycle boundaries. It intentionally opens a read-only connection without joining writable schema repair, journal setup, checkpoints, or permission mutation.

## User Impact

QA Smoke no longer reports a post-success unhandled rejection caused by its own teardown order. Runtime behavior outside QA Lab is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Exact-head architecture gate on `b0893f4203e7352d83f6c12c999be388a44abc3d`: passed, including Kysely guardrails and database-first legacy-store checks.
- Exact-head focused QA extension suite: 29 passed.
- Exact-head QA smoke on the QA Lab gateway plus `qa-channel` transport: `channel-chat-baseline` passed 1/1; output reached `CRABBOX_PHASE:complete` with `TEARDOWN_REJECTION:absent`.
- Remote proof ran from content-verified source synced to DigitalOcean Crabbox (`provider=digitalocean`, lease `cbx_16a7892bd40b`, Node 24.18, public networking, Tailscale disabled); the lease was deleted after validation.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh autoreview reported no accepted or actionable findings.

## Limitations

The full extension test-type project was not green locally because current main had unrelated iMessage nullability errors during the initial repair. The exact-head remote proof above covers this PR's changed behavior and the CI failure repaired here.

target.title: feat(web): show session branch row for local changed files
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The chat view already pins PR chips above the composer, and a pre-PR "Create PR" branch row — but that row only appears once the session's branch is pushed to origin and ahead of the default branch. A session that has changed files locally (uncommitted edits, untracked files, or unpushed commits) shows nothing, so there is no signal that the session produced work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Sessions with pending local work should surface it the same way pushed branches do. The gateway now emits the branch payload whenever the working tree has changed files vs the default-branch merge base (tracked via `git diff --shortstat`, plus untracked files). `createUrl` is withheld until GitHub's `pull/new` page actually has something to compare (branch pushed and ahead), so the row never links to a 404/"nothing to compare" page; the Control UI renders the Create PR link only when `createUrl` is present.

## User Impact

- A session on a git checkout with a GitHub remote now shows the branch row (repo, branch, +/− diff stats) as soon as it has changed files — committed, uncommitted, or untracked — instead of only after a push.
- The Create PR button still appears exactly when GitHub can open a PR (pushed branch with commits to compare).
- No change for sessions on the default branch, detached HEADs, non-git checkouts, or clean worktrees.

## Evidence

- Gateway: `src/gateway/control-ui-session-prs.test.ts` — new coverage for unpushed-branch-with-local-commit and pushed-but-nothing-to-compare-with-dirty-worktree, both asserting the row without `createUrl`; existing clean-tree cases still omit the row.
- UI: `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-pull-requests.test.ts` — branch row without `createUrl` renders stats and no Create PR link.
- Focused tests green on Blacksmith Testbox (gateway-core + ui shards), `pnpm check:changed` green remotely (including the TypeScript LOC ratchet, which forced a small tightening pass on the legacy file).
- Codex autoreview (gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh): one finding — "conflict-only trees report 0 files changed via shortstat" — rejected with an empirical repro: `git diff --shortstat <mergeBase>` diffs working-tree contents against the explicit base and does count unmerged paths (unlike bare `git diff`); invariant documented inline.
- Docs updated: `docs/web/control-ui.md` branch-row paragraph.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers can help update the branch when needed.

## What Problem This Solves

`memory_search` calls during an in-flight QMD reindex raced the pending update against a referenced 500ms timer. When the update settled first, the losing timer stayed alive until its deadline. Repeated searches could therefore stack pending handles and retain event-loop interest unnecessarily.

## Why This Change Was Made

The wait helper now owns and clears its timer in `finally`. This is the narrow owner boundary: both resolution and rejection of the pending update release the losing timer, while the timeout-first behavior remains unchanged.

Maintainer improvement: replaced the ambient process-resource-count assertion with an exact `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` handle lifecycle test. Twenty alternating resolve/reject iterations now prove every timer created by this method is cleared without depending on unrelated process timers.

## User Impact

**Before:** fast pending-update settlement left its losing 500ms timer referenced.

**After:** the timer is cleared immediately after either race outcome settles. Search timing and the 500ms upper bound remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Exact maintainer head: `4780a8c2cfa5c2badaa1fa0f78727d43466d7d8c`.
- Initial Testbox: focused memory-core regression suite, 150 tests passed; `check:changed` passed. Run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29269035521

Fix classification: root-cause timer lifecycle repair. No schema, config, protocol, provider, or migration surface changes.

target.title: ci: scope PR Node tests to changed targets
target.body:
Closes #106511

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary pull requests launch the full 14-job compact Node matrix even when a small, precisely testable surface changed. This adds runner-registration pressure and delays useful CI feedback.

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical pull requests now reuse the changed-test resolver against the synthetic merged tree and run one targeted Node job when the result is precise. Each selected test file retains process isolation. Broad, renamed, deleted, package, public plugin SDK, special-setup, whole-config, unmatched, planner-failed, oversized-path, and more-than-20-target plans fail safe to the existing compact full suite. Main, manual, and release runs remain full.

The review finding about indirect public SDK consumers is addressed with import-graph reachability across both normal imports and re-exports. A core source change that flows into a public SDK entry now falls back to the compact full suite, covering package-specifier consumers that the relative import graph cannot see. Unresolved non-test targets also fail safe instead of borrowing an unrelated directory test.

Every changed path must independently resolve before the aggregate targeted plan is accepted, preventing precise files from masking global or unknown paths. Targeted plans also retain the full built-artifact boundary gate because repository-wide scanners cannot be discovered from the import graph.

Busy-main validation drift was repaired and landed separately in #106751. A later Lobster contract regression is covered by an explicit computed-runtime dependency declaration. This branch is rebased onto the current-main baseline.

## User Impact

Common focused pull requests register one Node test runner instead of 14, reducing queue pressure and feedback time. Risky or ambiguous changes retain current coverage and fan-out. No runtime product behavior changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where session-list clients must reverse-engineer opaque routing keys such as `agent:main:telegram:main:direct:…` to render a useful session picker. That leaks Gateway-internal naming rules into every client and makes it easy to expose peer or machine identifiers.

Session clients can show readable labels such as “Main session,” “Telegram direct message,” “Scheduled task,” or a user-defined label while consistently separating foreground conversations from heartbeat, cron, subagent, ACP, hook, harness, dreaming, and other background sessions.

target.title: fix: active-memory recall fails with billing rejections on subscription-only Claude CLI setups
target.body:
Closes #106839
Related: #86761

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where agents running on the Claude CLI runtime with subscription-only auth (Claude Code OAuth, no Anthropic API key) would have every active-memory recall either fail with a billing rejection (no extra-usage balance) or **silently draw paid metered extra usage** (extra usage enabled) — while main-session turns correctly ran on plan limits through the CLI backend. Anthropic routing direct anthropic-messages calls on subscription tokens to extra-usage billing is long-standing behavior; the embedded runner's direct-API passthrough (`cli_runtime_passthrough_openclaw`) was never a viable path for these credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an opt-in `RunEmbeddedAgentParams.cliBackendDispatch: "subscription-auth"`: when the run's provider is `claude-cli` — directly or via a canonical `anthropic/<model>` ref whose configured `agentRuntime` is claude-cli — a backend is registered, and the ordered credential selection resolves to subscription (oauth/token) or nothing rather than an API key, the run executes through `runCliAgent` as a one-shot turn. Active-memory recall opts in. The dispatch preserves the embedded run's contracts:

- **Tool restriction is enforced server-side**: `toolsAllow` maps to the selectable-backend surface, bounds the loopback MCP grant (tools outside it can be neither listed nor called, even under bypass permission modes), and restricted runs get an exclusive loopback-only MCP bundle — user/plugin MCP servers are not merged in.
- **Transcript parity**: the run is mirrored into the caller-owned session file (user turn, live tool call/result records, assistant snapshot — flushed immediately on abort), so `persistTranscripts`, timeout partial-text salvage, and the live terminal-search watcher work identically to embedded runs.
- **Isolation**: fresh CLI process per run, no live-session reuse, session-scoped MCP cleanup (never the process-wide loopback server), CLI session bindings dropped from the result.
- **Scope**: claude-cli only; `google-gemini-cli` and custom backends keep the passthrough — their direct-API contracts were not verified and this PR makes no claims about them. An available API key keeps the existing fast passthrough. The core-side provider set could move to a `CliBackendConfig` capability flag if maintainers prefer that seam.

## User Impact

Subscription-only Claude CLI deployments get working active-memory recall on plan limits, consistent with their main turns — instead of failing every turn or silently consuming paid extra usage. Setups with an Anthropic API key see no behavior change. No config changes required; note that CLI-dispatched recalls measured 13.8–16.9s on a dev laptop, so the plugin's default 15s `timeoutMs` is tight — 30s is comfortable.

## Summary
- redact exec foreground tool-result text and structured `details.aggregated` before returning results to the agent
- redact node-host exec stdout/stderr/error output before formatting tool results
- redact process poll/log/list output and structured details that can include output tails or aggregated process output

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** Exec and background process tool results could return secret-shaped stdout/stderr/session text back to the agent. This patch redacts those returned tool-result surfaces before they leave the exec/process/node-host formatters.

**Real environment tested:** Real local OpenClaw checkout on branch `fix/exec-tool-result-redaction` at `da701a0bbf6c`, using an isolated temporary `OPENCLAW_HOME`. The proof used an obvious fake canary value, not a real credential.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran a local runtime proof that exercised `createExecTool` and `createProcessTool` with a fake `REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET` value, then inspected the returned tool-result `content[0].text` and structured `details.aggregated` values for foreground exec, process poll, process log, and process list tail/details surfaces.

**Evidence after fix:** Copied live output from the local runtime proof:

```json
{
  "foregroundExec": {
    "status": "completed",
    "text": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890",
    "detailsAggregated": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890",
    "rawCanaryValuePresent": false,
    "redactedMarkerPresent": true
  },
  "processPoll": {
    "status": "completed",
    "text": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890\n\n\nProcess exited with code 0.",
    "detailsAggregated": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890\n",
    "rawCanaryValuePresent": false,
    "redactedMarkerPresent": true
  },
  "processLog": {
    "status": "completed",
    "text": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890",
    "detailsAggregated": "",
    "rawCanaryValuePresent": false,
    "redactedMarkerPresent": true
  },
  "processList": {
    "status": "completed",
    "textTail": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890",
    "rawCanaryValuePresent": false,
    "redactedMarkerPresent": true
  }
}
```

Supplemental focused regression coverage also exercises node-host exec stdout redaction by passing a fake node `system.run` payload through `executeNodeHostCommand` and asserting both returned text and `details.aggregated` redact the raw canary.

**Observed result after fix:** The raw fake canary value was absent from returned foreground exec, process poll, process log, and process list output. Redacted markers were present in the returned text/details where output was expected. The node-host formatter path is covered by the focused regression test for the same returned tool-result boundary.

**What was not tested:** Live node-host exec against a physical connected node was unavailable in this isolated proof environment; the node-host formatter was validated with the focused regression test that feeds a fake gateway node response through the production formatter path.

The new redaction regression tests pass individually under the agents-core Vitest config.

- Added commit `bc79136bb7` to redact background exec `details.tail` before returning running-session tool results.
