target.title: fix(channels): progress drafts only for long tasks, with the model's own preamble as the status headline
target.body:
Closes #105872

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes progress drafts appearing for small tasks even though the draft gate nominally waits five seconds. The second work event bypassed that delay, and the utility narrator could spend a model call before any draft was visible. Progress-mode channels also discarded the model's typed preamble even though it is the most accurate status headline available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The draft gate is now purely time-based; explicit immediate paths such as approvals and patches remain immediate. Utility narration starts only after the draft becomes visible. The shared compositor prefers fresh, typed model preambles as the headline, then uses utility narration only when the preamble is absent or stale. No config or model-facing tool surface was added.

The implementation preserves preamble item identity and retractions, counts only sanitized commentary that the compositor accepts, cancels narrator retries and expiry timers when a turn settles, rejects stale in-flight utility results, resets queued-turn lifecycle state, and refreshes same-text headlines when a new preamble item arrives.

## User Impact

- Fast turns produce only the final answer: no transient draft, receipt, or utility narration call.
- Long turns show the model's current preamble as the status headline, with utility narration filling genuine silences and tool activity retained below it.
- Retractions clear the matching headline, final delivery removes the draft, and queued turns begin with fresh lifecycle state.

target.title: fix(tools-manager): use BigInt for lossless Content-Length comparison
target.body:
## Summary
Replace `Number()` + `isSafeInteger` with `BigInt()` for lossless Content-Length comparison in `downloadFile`.

## What Problem This Solves
`Number()` can lose precision when parsing large integer strings (≥16 digits). The existing `CONTENT_LENGTH_RE` regex `/^\d+$/` matches arbitrarily long digit strings with no upper bound, but `Number("9007199254740993")` returns `9007199254740992` — a different value.

Although `isSafeInteger` catches most precision-loss cases (any value that rounds above `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`), relying on `Number()` for integer comparison is fragile. A Content-Length string of 20+ digits like `"99999999999999999999"` becomes `100000000000000000000` through `Number()` — completely wrong.

In practice `MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES` is 100 MB (~10⁸), so any oversized Content-Length is caught by the numeric comparison long before precision becomes an issue. This is a **correctness hardening** — using the right tool (`BigInt`) for integer comparison so the code is obviously correct at all scales.

**Code evidence**: in `src/agents/utils/tools-manager.ts:187-188`, the current code parses Content-Length through `Number()` which is not guaranteed lossless for arbitrary-length digit strings.

## Root Cause
The code was written using `Number()` for integer parsing, which is lossy for values beyond 2⁵³ − 1 (`Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` = 9,007,199,254,740,991). The `isSafeInteger` guard partially mitigates this but:
1. It rejects values for the wrong reason (precision loss vs size cap)
2. The error message says "exceeds byte limit" when actually the value can't be accurately parsed
3. It relies on an indirect property (safe integer vs range check) rather than comparing the value directly

## Why This Fix
**Chosen approach**: `BigInt(contentLength) > BigInt(maxBytes)` — one-line replacement.

- **Correct**: `BigInt` preserves the exact integer from any digit string
- **Simpler**: replaces two conditions (`!isSafeInteger || > maxBytes`) with one (`> maxBytes`)
- **Proven**: `BigInt` is already used elsewhere in the codebase (`src/infra/kysely-sync.ts` etc.)
- **Minimal**: 2 lines removed, 1 line added

Alternatives considered:
- String length pre-check: avoids the problem but is ad-hoc
- `BigInt` + fallback: unnecessary — `BigInt` is well-supported in Node 22

## User Impact
No user-visible change. The existing behavior was already correct for all practical Content-Length values (≤ a few GB). This fix hardens the code against theoretically large Content-Length headers and makes the intent clearer.

## Evidence
- **Before (Number() approach)**: `Number("9007199254740993")` → `9007199254740992` (precision LOST). `Number("99999999999999999999")` → `100000000000000000000` (massively wrong). ❌ FAIL
- **After (BigInt() approach)**: `BigInt("9007199254740993")` → `9007199254740993n` (exact). `BigInt("99999999999999999999")` → `99999999999999999999n` (exact). ✓ PASS

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (Number() approach — precision loss)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
============================================================
Content-Length precision loss demonstration
============================================================
Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER = 9007199254740991

--- Case 1: Large Content-Length (above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) ---
Content-Length header: "9007199254740993"
Number("9007199254740993") = 9007199254740992
Actual BigInt value : 9007199254740993
Precision preserved?  : NO — LOST!

Old code (Number + isSafeInteger):
  declaredBytes = Number("9007199254740993") = 9007199254740992
  isSafeInteger(9007199254740992) = false
  => REJECT (declaredBytes=9007199254740992, reason="exceeds cap or not safe integer")

--- Case 3: 20-digit Content-Length ---
Number("99999999999999999999") = 100000000000000000000
Number result accurate?  NO — massively wrong!

FAIL: Number() lost precision on Content-Length '9007199254740993'
FAIL: Number() returned wrong value for 20-digit Content-Length
```

### After (BigInt() comparison — exact)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
--- Case 1: Large Content-Length (above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) ---
New code (BigInt comparison):
  BigInt("9007199254740993") = 9007199254740993n
  9007199254740993n > 10n = true
  => REJECT (reason="exceeds cap")

--- Case 2: Normal Content-Length (within safe range) ---
Old: ACCEPT  |  New: ACCEPT

PASS: BigInt() preserves exact value: 9007199254740993n
```

## Tests and Validation
- `pnpm check` passed
- `vitest run src/agents/utils/tools-manager.test.ts` — 18 tests passed (2 new: large Content-Length rejection)
- Added regression test: "rejects downloads with large Content-Length that would lose precision with Number()"

target.title: fix: restore GitHub Copilot turns and account context limits
target.body:
Closes #106170

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users selecting GitHub Copilot models could receive a `network connection error` after runtime token exchange, before the model request reached GitHub.

The same path could use synthetic 128K model limits instead of the selected account's live catalog limits, and could retain another profile's limits during profile rotation, direct-auth fallback, or compaction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The complete fix keeps runtime credentials refreshable while ensuring OpenClaw selects its managed provider transport whenever exchanged auth is available. GitHub Copilot live catalogs and cached exchanged tokens are scoped to the source credential/profile, and normal plus compaction paths rematerialize model metadata whenever the active credential changes.

Cross-provider compaction only reuses a forwarded profile when its prepared auth plan matches the target provider/model. Route-less profile handling is gated by the provider's existing `preferRuntimeResolvedModel` ownership hook, so unrelated Claude CLI/PI auth overlays retain their current behavior.

## User Impact

GitHub Copilot turns now reach the provider after token exchange, token refreshes remain effective during long tool loops, and long-context budgeting reflects the active account. target.title: fix(skills): globally-installed ClawHub skills falsely show as not tracked [AI-assisted]
target.body:
> [AI-assisted] This PR was generated using Claude Code.

Closes #105530

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who install a ClawHub skill **globally** (`openclaw skills install <slug> --global`, living under the managed dir `~/.openclaw/skills/<slug>` and tracked in the **global** lockfile `~/.openclaw/.clawhub/lock.json`) would see the skill falsely reported as `ClawHub link invalid` in `openclaw skills status` and the Control UI, with the message:

> Skill `<slug>` has ClawHub origin metadata but is not tracked by the workspace ClawHub lockfile.

The skill is in fact correctly installed and tracked - just in the global lockfile, not the workspace one.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` read the ClawHub lockfile exclusively from the workspace directory (`readClawHubSkillsLockfileStatusSync(workspaceDir)`) and passed that single read to `resolveClawHubSkillStatusLinkSync` for every non-bundled skill. For a globally-installed skill (`source: "openclaw-managed"`), the tracking entry lives in the **managed** lockfile at `<dirname(managedSkillsDir)>/.clawhub/lock.json`, so the workspace lookup misses it and returns `invalid`.

The fix resolves the link status for `openclaw-managed` skills against the managed lockfile (and the managed parent dir, so the expected-install-dir check matches the skill dir) instead of the workspace lockfile. Workspace-local skills are unchanged. Detection uses the loader-assigned `source` rather than a lexical path check, because managed skill roots may contain symlinks whose resolved `baseDir` sits outside the `managedSkillsDir` tree.

## User Impact

Globally installed ClawHub skills now show as correctly `linked` in `openclaw skills status` and the Control UI skills view, instead of a false `ClawHub link invalid` / "not tracked" warning. Workspace-local skill status is unaffected.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof captured on Windows 10 by running the production `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` against real on-disk lockfiles (standalone `tsx` repro script run locally; before/after output below). The script creates a managed (global) install - skill dir under `managedSkillsDir` with `.clawhub/origin.json`, plus a global lockfile at `<managedParent>/.clawhub/lock.json` tracking it - and a separate workspace whose own lockfile does **not** track the skill.

BEFORE (unpatched main) - the globally-installed skill is falsely `invalid`, read against the **workspace** lockfile:

```
"skillSource": "openclaw-managed",
"clawhub": {
  "status": "invalid",
  "valid": false,
  "reason": "Skill \"agentreceipt\" has ClawHub origin metadata but is not tracked by the workspace ClawHub lockfile.",
  "slug": "agentreceipt",
  "lockPath": "...\\openclaw-workspace-fYctHw\\.clawhub\\lock.json"
}
```

AFTER (this patch) - the same skill is correctly `linked`, read against the **managed (global)** lockfile:

```
"skillSource": "openclaw-managed",
"clawhub": {
  "status": "linked",
  "valid": true,
  "registry": "https://clawhub.ai",
  "slug": "agentreceipt",
  "installedVersion": "1.2.3",
  "lockPath": "...\\openclaw-managed-83CHpB\\.clawhub\\lock.json"
}
```

Regression tests added in `src/skills/discovery/status.test.ts`:
- links a globally-installed skill via the managed lockfile (asserts `status: "linked"`)
- reports a globally-installed skill as `invalid` when it is absent from the managed lockfile (guards against falsely linking)

Full skill-status suite passes (`pnpm test -- src/skills/discovery/status.test.ts` -> 13 passed, 1 skipped on win32).

## Real Behavior Proof

- Behavior addressed: Globally installed ClawHub skills (`source: "openclaw-managed"`) are falsely reported as `invalid` / "not tracked by the workspace ClawHub lockfile" because `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` only consults the workspace lockfile.
- Real environment tested: Windows 10, Node v22.22.3, OpenClaw main @ 50e5ffcd25, running the production `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` function from `src/skills/discovery/status.ts` via `pnpm exec tsx`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: a standalone `tsx` script builds a managed/global install (skill dir + `.clawhub/origin.json` + global lockfile tracking the slug) and a separate workspace whose lockfile omits the slug, then calls `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus(workspaceDir, { managedSkillsDir, entries })` and prints the resolved `clawhub` status.
- Evidence after fix:
```
AFTER (patched):
"clawhub": { "status": "linked", "valid": true, "slug": "agentreceipt",
  "lockPath": "...\\openclaw-managed-83CHpB\\.clawhub\\lock.json" }

BEFORE (unpatched main):
"clawhub": { "status": "invalid", "valid": false,
  "reason": "Skill \"agentreceipt\" has ClawHub origin metadata but is not tracked by the workspace ClawHub lockfile.",
  "lockPath": "...\\openclaw-workspace-fYctHw\\.clawhub\\lock.json" }
```
- Observed result after fix: The globally-installed skill resolves to `status: "linked"` against the managed (global) lockfile instead of `invalid` against the workspace lockfile. The `lockPath` in the resolved status now points at the global lockfile.
- What was not tested: End-to-end through a running gateway / live Control UI render; the real `openclaw skills status` CLI against a real `~/.openclaw` home. The proof exercises the real production status function with real on-disk lockfiles, which is the exact code path the CLI and UI consume.

## Human Verification

Verified: the production `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` code path with real on-disk managed + workspace lockfiles (before/after), scoped `pnpm test` for the skills status suite, `pnpm tsgo` (type check), `pnpm format:check`, scoped `oxlint --type-aware` on the changed files. Not verified: Swift (skipped on Windows), full `pnpm test` suite, live Control UI rendering. Note: local `pnpm build` (tsdown) hit a V8 out-of-memory crash on this Windows machine (a known low-memory local-env quirk, unrelated to this 3-line logic change); relying on CI's build check on a properly-sized runner.

## Security Impact

- Does this change authentication, authorization, or trust boundaries? No.
- Does this change credential, secret, or token handling? No.
- Does this change sandboxing or process isolation? No.
- Does this change network boundaries or external API calls? No.
- Does this introduce a new trust boundary or change an existing one? No.

No CODEOWNERS secops paths are touched (`src/skills/` is not secops-owned). The change only affects which local lockfile is consulted for a status display.

## Compatibility / Migration

No config, API, CLI, or lockfile-format changes. The set of inputs/outputs of `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` is unchanged; only the accuracy of the `clawhub` status for globally-installed skills improves. No migration required.

## Failure Recovery

If the managed lockfile read regresses, globally-installed skills would revert to the prior `invalid` / "not tracked" display behavior - a cosmetic status misreport, not a crash or data loss. The change is read-only with respect to lockfiles (no writes), so there is no risk of lockfile corruption. Reverting the commit fully restores prior behavior.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Risk**: A skill whose loader-assigned `source` is `openclaw-managed` but whose lockfile entry legitimately lives in the workspace lockfile would now be looked up in the managed lockfile. **Mitigation**: managed skills are, by definition, installed under `managedSkillsDir` and tracked in the managed lockfile; workspace-local skills use other `source` values and are unaffected. Added a regression test for the "absent from managed lockfile" case to ensure such a skill still reports `invalid` rather than falsely `linked`.
- **Risk**: Competing/sibling PR on the same issue. **Mitigation**: this PR supplies the real-behavior-proof (real production-function output with real on-disk lockfiles, before/after) that the issue's proof gate requires, rather than a screenshot.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I will respond to review comments in the review conversation where they were left.
- [x] I understand review conversations belong to the reviewer and I should not resolve them myself unless requested.

target.title: fix(ai): safely format circular rejections in stream catch paths
target.body:
Closes #106570
Related: #106568

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where provider stream failure handling could throw a second exception when formatting a non-Error rejection that contains circular references. That second throw prevented a clean terminal error event and stream end on OpenAI Completions (and the sibling Google shared stream path), so agent runs could hang or fail without a structured provider error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Introduces a shared `formatUnknownError` helper that prefers `Error.message`, safely JSON-stringifies ordinary values, falls back to `String(error)` when `JSON.stringify` throws, and returns the constant `"Unknown error"` if `String()` itself throws (null-prototype or hostile conversion hooks). The OpenAI Completions, Google shared, and Anthropic stream catch paths use it so terminal stream termination cannot be broken by circular or hostile rejection payloads. OpenAI Responses/Azure already guarded stringify; this keeps the unsafe catch sites consistent without new config or fallback policy.

Fix quality: compatibility — no API/config shape change, same errorMessage field; performance — O(1) catch-path only; usability — still delivers a terminal error message; security — no secret logging or trust-boundary changes.

## User Impact

When a provider transport rejects with an unusual non-Error object (including circular structures or values whose String conversion throws), the agent stream fails closed with a normal error stop reason and message instead of throwing inside the recovery path.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Node v24.17.0)

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/utils/format-unknown-error.test.ts
# 4 passed (Error.message, JSON path, circular String fallback, non-throwing final literal)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts \
  packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.test.ts \
  -t "circular"
# 2 passed (OpenAI #106570 + Google #106568 lifecycle: stopReason=error + non-empty errorMessage)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts -t "circular" --reporter=verbose
# ✓ emits a terminal error for circular non-Error rejections without rethrowing (#106570)

pnpm exec oxfmt --check packages/ai/src/utils/format-unknown-error.ts \
  packages/ai/src/utils/format-unknown-error.test.ts  # pass
git diff --check  # pass
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Stream catch paths must emit a terminal error event when the transport rejects with a circular non-Error value (or a value whose String conversion throws), without a second exception in the recovery path.
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout; focused Vitest via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`; Node v24.17.0 runtime transcript for the formatter + stream-shaped terminal events. No live provider credentials required (SDK circular non-Error shapes are not guaranteed from supported providers; proof exercises the catch-path contract the providers call).
- Current-main contrast: On main, `error instanceof Error ? error.message : JSON.stringify(error)` throws `TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON` for self-referential objects, so the catch path never reaches `stream.push({ type: "error" })` / `stream.end()`. Reproduced with: `const c={k:1}; c.self=c; JSON.stringify(c)` → throws.
- Exact steps after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/utils/format-unknown-error.test.ts`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts -t "circular"`
  3. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.test.ts -t "circular"`
  4. Runtime transcript (formatter + stream-shaped terminal emission; redacted, no secrets):
```text
=== formatUnknownError runtime proof (redacted) ===
host: darwin v24.17.0
before: JSON.stringify(circular) throws: true
format(circular): threw=false value="[object Object]"
format(null-proto-circular): threw=false value="Unknown error"
format(hostile-circular): threw=false value="Unknown error"
format(Error): threw=false value="upstream boom"
format(plain-object): threw=false value="{\"code\":\"ECONNRESET\"}"

=== stream catch-path terminal emission (synthetic runtime, OpenAI Completions shape) ===
case=circular-non-Error
  output.stopReason= error
  output.errorMessage= [object Object]
  events= [{"type":"error","reason":"error","errorMessage":"[object Object]"},{"type":"end"}]
  stream_closed= true
case=null-proto-circular
  output.stopReason= error
  output.errorMessage= Unknown error
  events= [{"type":"error","reason":"error","errorMessage":"Unknown error"},{"type":"end"}]
  stream_closed= true
case=hostile-circular
  output.stopReason= error
  output.errorMessage= Unknown error
  events= [{"type":"error","reason":"error","errorMessage":"Unknown error"},{"type":"end"}]
  stream_closed= true
proof_ok=true
```
- Evidence after fix: Focused OpenAI/Google lifecycle cases pass with `stopReason === "error"` and a non-empty `errorMessage`. Helper never throws: circular → `[object Object]`; null-prototype/hostile circular → `"Unknown error"`. Runtime events show `{type:"error"}` then stream end for each case.
- Control check: Ordinary Error rejections still use `error.message`; ordinary plain objects still JSON-stringify; only circular non-Errors take the String fallback; only values that break both JSON and String take the constant literal.
- Observed result after fix: Circular and hostile non-Error rejections produce a terminal stream error instead of a secondary serialization/conversion crash.
- What was not tested: Live OpenAI/Google network failures that happen to reject with circular non-Error SDK payloads; Anthropic live path (same helper wired for sibling invariant only).

---

AI-assisted contribution: implementation and tests authored with AI assistance (Grok). Proof commands and results above were run on this host.

target.title: fix(gateway): recover when suppressed channel secrets are unavailable
target.body:
Closes #106379

Supersedes #106405. That PR identifies the same startup ordering bug, but its
implementation removes channels from the secrets runtime `sourceConfig`. This
change instead keeps the complete source config recoverable while using a
separate assignment projection for the already-suppressed startup path.

AI-assisted: yes. The runtime path, source/assignment snapshot contract, tests,
and service proof were reviewed before submission.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where supervised Gateway users could remain in a restart loop
after the persisted crash-loop breaker had already suppressed channel
autostart. An unavailable SecretRef on a suppressed channel was still resolved
during eager startup preflight, so the Gateway exited before its control plane
became available.

The earlier candidate in #106405 avoids that startup failure by pruning the
channel surface from the source config itself. That loses the complete channel
configuration from the active secrets snapshot, so the runtime no longer owns
the source needed to restore normal channel assignment projection after the
credential becomes available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing breaker decision is passed into the secrets activator before
startup projection. During breaker-suppressed startup only, the activator:

- preserves the complete config as `sourceConfig`;
- passes a channel-free `assignmentConfig` into SecretRef projection;
- keeps Gateway authentication and every non-channel required secret
  fail-closed; and
- applies no suppression to reload or restart-check projections.

This uses the existing secrets runtime source/assignment split rather than
mutating process-wide skip state or permanently deleting channels from the
runtime source config.

## User Impact

After the crash-loop breaker trips, a missing credential on an already-
suppressed channel no longer keeps the entire Gateway in a supervisor restart
loop. The authenticated control plane can start for diagnosis and repair.

Normal startup remains fail-loud, Gateway authentication remains fail-closed,
and a later reload can project the preserved channel configuration again after
the channel credential is repaired.

## Evidence

Current code base:

- Official base: `b4343426f11e949c6483c1ab552e762883bb3b2e`
- Changed surface: `src/gateway/server-startup-config.ts`,
  `src/gateway/server.impl.ts`, focused startup SecretRef tests, and
  `src/gateway/server-startup-config.breaker-secrets.integration.test.ts`
- Local lightweight checks: targeted `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check`
  passed

Focused regression coverage verifies:

- breaker-suppressed startup projects no channel assignments;
- the prepared snapshot retains the full channel-bearing `sourceConfig`;
- normal startup still projects channels;
- Gateway auth SecretRefs still resolve and remain required;
- reload after suppressed startup restores full channel assignment projection;
  and
- `prepareGatewayStartupConfig()` uses the same source/assignment boundary.

Pre-submission generated-systemd proof passed all jobs on the predecessor
candidate, including before-fix restart-loop reproduction, after-fix
convergence, fail-closed Gateway-auth behavior, focused/adjacent tests, and the
changed-file gate:

- [Pre-submission systemd proof](https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29275306932)

An exact-head CI and generated-systemd proof run for this PR head will be linked
here before the PR is marked ready for review.

## Risk And Rollback

The behavior change is limited to `reason: "startup"` when the persisted
breaker has already selected channel autostart suppression. Explicit skip
environment behavior remains unchanged, and reload/restart-check paths retain
the full assignment projection. Reverting this commit restores the previous
startup behavior without a config or data migration.

target.title: feat: publish linux/riscv64 Docker images
target.body:
Related: #11977
Prior art: #12033 (my earlier attempt, which the stale bot closed for inactivity)

> AI-assisted: I drafted and built this with Claude Code, then verified it by hand on real riscv64 hardware (see Evidence). I understand what the code does.

## What Problem This Solves

There is no riscv64 OpenClaw image today, so anyone on a RISC-V board (SpaceMiT K1 and friends) can't `docker pull` OpenClaw the way amd64 and arm64 users can. The catch is that the official `node:24-bookworm` base has no riscv64 variant, so you can't just add the platform to the existing matrix and call it done.

## Why This Change Was Made

A separate `Dockerfile.riscv64` deals with the two things that make riscv64 different:

- The runtime is built on `debian:trixie-slim` with Node.js from unofficial-builds, because no `node:24-bookworm` riscv64 image exists.
- rolldown ships no riscv64 binary, so the JS bundle is cross-built on the host arch and only the native addons install natively on riscv64.

The build is QEMU-emulated and therefore slow, so `build-riscv64` is `continue-on-error` and never blocks a release. A follow-up `update-manifest` job folds the riscv64 child into the default `:version`/`:latest`/`:main` tags after attestation verification, and only when the riscv64 build actually produced a digest. Slim and browser tags stay amd64+arm64. The riscv64 child has no SLSA attestation (it's emulated, `provenance: false`), which is why it gets folded in after the amd64/arm64 attestation check rather than before.

I kept it fully additive so a red riscv64 build can't touch the existing release. If you'd rather ship the riscv64 tag standalone and not fold it into `:latest`, that's an easy change, so let me know if you'd prefer that.

## User Impact

On riscv64 hardware both of these work:

```
docker pull ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:<version>-riscv64
docker pull ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:<version>   # multi-arch, now includes riscv64
```

There's also a new "RISC-V (linux/riscv64)" section in `docs/install/docker.md` covering the quick start, the container auth requirement, and the known limits.

## Evidence

Built via QEMU on an x86 host, then run natively on a Banana Pi BPI-F3 (SpaceMiT K1, riscv64):

- `node openclaw.mjs gateway` reaches `[gateway] ready` with all 10 bundled plugins loaded (acpx, anthropic, browser, canvas, device-pair, file-transfer, memory-core, ollama, phone-control, talk-voice).
- `GET /healthz` returns `200 {"ok":true,"status":"live"}`
- `GET /readyz` returns `200 {"ready":true,"failing":[]}`
- `process.arch` is `riscv64`, version `OpenClaw 2026.7.2`, and the node-pty native addon loads.
- One gotcha I hit and documented: inside a container the gateway binds to `0.0.0.0` and refuses to start without auth, so you have to set `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN`.

Build validation:

- A parity build with the same extensions the amd64/arm64 jobs use (`OPENCLAW_EXTENSIONS=diagnostics-otel,codex`) completes, and the image reports `OpenClaw 2026.7.2` / `riscv64 linux`.
- `docker-release.yml` passes yamllint and actionlint.

## Notes and limits

- No slim or browser variant for riscv64.
- No browser automation, since Chromium has no riscv64 build.
- I don't have Docker Hub secrets or the `docker-release` environment on my fork, so I couldn't run the full release workflow end to end there. The riscv64 build and run are validated as above; the workflow changes are validated by lint plus the local emulated build.

target.title: fix(acpx): stop creating empty stderr logs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ACP operators accumulated an empty stderr log file for every quiet Codex ACP process lease. On a busy long-running gateway this produced tens of thousands of zero-byte files without adding diagnostic value.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Codex auth bridge now creates the stderr log lazily on the first stderr write. Non-empty stderr remains captured exactly as before; quiet processes leave no file behind.

## User Impact

Operators can keep ACP stderr diagnostics enabled without unbounded zero-byte file churn. Existing non-empty diagnostics remain available for failures.

## Evidence

`pnpm test:extension acpx` passes all 155 tests on Node 24.18.0 after rebasing onto current `main`. The added tests cover both a quiet child process and a child that writes stderr.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Quiet ACP process leases created empty stderr log files even though there was no diagnostic output.
- **Real environment tested:** A Linux system running a long-lived OpenClaw gateway from a local build with the bundled ACPX extension and Codex ACP enabled.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Removed the existing empty lease logs, restarted the patched gateway, ran multiple quiet ACP turns, then triggered a run that emitted stderr and inspected the configured stderr log directory.
- **Evidence after fix:** Before the patch, the diagnostic directory contained approximately 29,590 zero-byte per-lease log files. After the patched quiet runs, zero new empty log files were created. The stderr-producing run created a non-empty retained log.
- **Observed result after fix:** Quiet ACP runs no longer create stderr files, while actual stderr output is still persisted for diagnosis.
- **What was not tested:** Windows and macOS process wrappers were not exercised in the real setup; their behavior is covered only by the shared implementation and automated tests.

## AI-assisted disclosure

This PR is AI-assisted. I ran the real behavior validation and automated tests myself, reviewed the diff, and understand that the change removes eager file creation while preserving append-on-stderr behavior.

target.title: fix(exec): memoize duplicate auto-review verdicts
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the exec approval path and understand the security boundary changed by this patch.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102249.

The model-backed exec auto-reviewer pays for a fresh reviewer completion whenever the same ask-requiring request is reviewed again. Retry, polling, and test loops can therefore turn N identical reviews into N paid model calls even though the reviewer runs deterministically at temperature 0.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a bounded per-reviewer-instance memo with conservative reuse semantics:

- cache only completed low-risk `allow-once` decisions
- key the memo on the full safety-relevant reviewer input, including `resolvedPath`
- force a fresh review when command, argv, resolved executable, cwd, environment keys, host, reason, analysis, or agent context changes
- never cache `ask`, timeout, unavailable-model, completion-error, or other conservative fallback outcomes
- cap the memo at 128 entries

The approval host still consumes each returned `allow-once` decision once. This patch does not persist decisions or change reviewer prompts, model routing, auth, or approval policy.

## User Impact

For N byte-identical requests within one reviewer instance, paid reviewer completions drop from N to 1. Changed executable resolution now explicitly remains a cache miss, preventing a verdict for one binary path from being reused for another.

## Evidence

Final rebase:

- `upstream/main`: `6315dd8e2da`
- branch head: `6b035127eed`

Commands run on this head:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts` -> passed, 23/23 tests
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.ts src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts` -> passed
- `git diff --check` -> passed
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main --timed` -> conflict, LOC, attribution, export, dependency, format, SDK baseline, package patch, temp-report, and core production typecheck gates passed; core-test typecheck was stopped after 934.31s under local resource pressure and is left to exact-head CI

Focused invariants:

- duplicate low-risk input: model completion count `2 -> 1`
- changed argv: fresh completion
- changed `resolvedPath`: fresh completion
- duplicate `ask`: two completions, no memo reuse

Known limit: a configured provider-backed billing run was not executed because it would require external credentials and incur model usage. The focused test exercises the production reviewer boundary with an injected completion dependency and asserts exact call counts.

target.title: feat(signal): add setup wizard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal setup needed a guided path that proves a usable receive transport before users rely on the channel, without OpenClaw creating or managing a Signal Docker container. Existing setup and status paths could also leave stale native/container transport fields ambiguous, miss account-specific API-mode behavior, or report a Signal daemon as generically working when the configured account was missing or receive was unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Signal plugin now owns a setup wizard for two supported transports: local `signal-cli` and an existing Signal server managed by the operator. The same change tightens native/container/auto probing so setup and status distinguish transport reachability from account and receive readiness, and it lets multi-account Signal configs use `channels.signal.apiMode` as a channel default with per-account overrides.

The shared setup contract gains one additive cancellation result so a plugin can refuse to persist an unusable setup. Cancellation discards wizard-local channel changes and skips later hooks and completion notes while preserving accepted external-plugin installation metadata. This contract is documented in the plugin SDK setup guide.

## User Impact

Users can run Signal setup, choose local `signal-cli` or an existing server URL, and save config only after the selected transport is reachable for the intended account. Operators get clearer `openclaw channels status --probe` and health output for ready, account-missing, receive-unavailable, and unreachable Signal states.

Existing/manual `bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api` deployments remain supported through `apiMode: "container"`. OpenClaw no longer offers an OpenClaw-managed Signal Docker setup path. Multi-account installations can mix native and container transports by overriding `apiMode` per account.

## Evidence

Behavioral proof:

- Native setup clears stale external/container endpoint fields at the intended account boundary while preserving explicit native bind settings.
- Existing-server setup probes the selected account before writing `httpUrl`, `autoStart: false`, and `apiMode: "auto"`.
- Native multi-account daemons are checked through `listAccounts`; bound single-account daemons remain supported through the upstream JSON-RPC method-not-found contract.
- Container receive readiness uses `/v1/receive/{account}`, and linked-account validation uses bounded `/v1/accounts` reads.
- Send, reaction, monitor, attachment, status, and probe paths resolve account-specific `apiMode` before the channel default.
- Setup cancellation rolls back wizard-local state but retains a successfully accepted external-plugin installation record.
- Native link guidance uses the saved `cliPath` and `configPath`, including home-relative paths containing spaces.
- Screenshots are omitted because this changes terminal setup, gateway status, config, docs, and tests rather than browser UI.

Automated proof on head `e3e20ca22bd360958ea60163dd5a5d1e9e4942f9`:

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxe3d3kgq03r6k68cj8n9gng`, Actions run `29264712583`, Node `25.9.0`.
- Full Signal suite passed: 35 files, 618 tests.
- Generic setup and cancellation tests passed: `src/channels/plugins/setup-wizard.test.ts` (1), `src/flows/channel-setup.test.ts` (19), and `src/commands/onboard-channels.e2e.test.ts` (17).
- Full `pnpm build` passed, including the SDK declaration graph, CLI bootstrap guard, and Control UI performance gate.
- Relevant `tsgo`, extension/core test-type, scoped oxlint, oxfmt, generated metadata/baseline, and `git diff --check` gates passed.
- `pnpm docs:list` and `pnpm docs:check-mdx` passed; the MDX check covered 725 files.

Review proof:

- Two consecutive independent native review passes on the exact final head found no actionable regressions.
- A fresh cold review of the exact frozen range found no actionable findings after checking setup ownership, runtime callers and siblings, tests, SDK cancellation docs, and direct upstream Signal contracts.
- The final best-solution judgment is to keep the change atomic: wizard persistence, readiness probing, per-account routing, and cancellation share one contract, while Signal-specific behavior remains in the Signal plugin.

target.title: fix(secrets): keep startup alive when TTS SecretRefs are missing
target.body:
Closes #101204

## What Problem This Solves

A configured but temporarily missing built-in TTS API-key SecretRef currently aborts Gateway startup, taking unrelated chat, auth, tools, channels, and plugins offline even though only speech synthesis needs that credential.

## Summary

A missing built-in TTS provider API-key SecretRef no longer prevents Gateway startup. The affected TTS provider remains unconfigured, a structured warning is emitted, and unrelated Gateway capabilities continue to start.

This is intentionally narrow: only a matching missing-value error for an active built-in TTS API-key assignment degrades. Invalid refs, provider policy/security failures, provider contract failures, mismatched errors, non-string resolved values, and all required credentials still fail closed.

## Breaking changes

None to config shape, RPC schema, persisted state, or package dependencies. This does change failure timing for one credential class: an absent built-in TTS API-key SecretRef is reported at startup as a warning and fails locally when that TTS provider is used, instead of aborting Gateway startup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Built-in TTS is an optional capability, but SecretRef activation previously treated its API keys like credentials required for the whole Gateway. The narrow cold-start exception keeps the shared secrets boundary strict for reload, restart-check, config-write preflight, malformed refs, policy/security failures, provider failures, and invalid resolved values.

## User Impact

Operators may keep an optional ElevenLabs or other built-in TTS SecretRef configured while its value is temporarily absent. Cold startup continues with that provider unconfigured; after the SecretRef is restored, the provider becomes usable through the normal config/runtime refresh path. Reload and config-write preflight still reject the unresolved ref and preserve the last-known-good snapshot/config.

## Implementation

- `src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.ts` marks only built-in TTS provider API-key assignments as optional at startup.
- `src/secrets/resolve-errors.ts` owns typed provider/ref errors and the missing-value classifier; `src/secrets/resolve.ts` assigns the narrow error codes at env/file/exec and provider-contract boundaries.
- `src/secrets/runtime-optional-assignments.ts` owns required/optional partitioning, independent optional resolution, warning emission, and redaction registration.
- `src/secrets/runtime-prepare.runtime.ts` exports that helper through the existing lazy startup facade, so the Gateway hot path does not statically load the resolver.
- `src/secrets/runtime.ts` delegates assignment resolution once and remains focused on snapshot preparation/activation.
- `src/secrets/runtime-shared.ts` carries optional-assignment metadata while retaining the existing resolved-value shape validation.

## Code-path analysis

- Runtime entry: `src/gateway/server-startup-config.ts` prepares the secrets snapshot before startup activation.
- Owner boundary: `src/secrets/runtime.ts` owns snapshot preparation and delegates assignment resolution through the lazy `src/secrets/runtime-prepare.runtime.ts` facade.
- Optional-assignment owner: `src/secrets/runtime-optional-assignments.ts` owns partitioning, resolution, warning, and redaction behavior without growing the snapshot/lifecycle module.
- Collector/caller: `src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors.ts` routes core/channel/plugin surfaces; TTS API keys are collected by `src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.ts` from top-level, agent, and channel voice TTS blocks.
- Resolver/callee: `src/secrets/resolve.ts` resolves env/file/exec refs; `src/secrets/resolve-errors.ts` classifies absence separately from policy/validation/provider/contract failures.
- Sibling invariant: gateway auth, model/provider, plugin, channel-token, and other required assignments continue through the required batch and remain fail-closed.
- Localized runtime failure: `src/gateway/server-methods/tts.ts` returns the normal provider-not-configured `UNAVAILABLE` path when the degraded provider is selected.
- Adjacent tests: `src/secrets/resolve.test.ts`, `src/secrets/runtime.test.ts`, `src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.test.ts`, `src/secrets/runtime-discord-surface.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-startup-config.secrets.test.ts`, and `src/gateway/server-methods/tts.test.ts`.

## Mainline comparison

Rebased onto `OpenClaw/OpenClaw:main@5f3d56a2f022288bc020c5c93594652c31ad21eb` (commit time 2026-07-13T18:26:18Z; fetched 2026-07-13T18:27Z).

The same-surface upstream change since the earlier review base was `93b3f4c45b` (`feat(xai): add native streaming TTS`), which updates xAI speech implementation/tests and `docs/tools/tts.md` but does not change the SecretRef collector, resolver, startup snapshot boundary, or localized provider-not-configured contract. Later Gateway changes through `5f3d56a2f0` modify restart and chat dispatch lifecycle files but do not touch secrets snapshot preparation or TTS.

## Branch / base provenance

- Base: `OpenClaw/OpenClaw:main@5f3d56a2f022288bc020c5c93594652c31ad21eb`
- Head: `snowzlmbot/OpenClaw:fix/optional-tts-secret-startup@b89582184f0c6612a8187aa00f9416a30faec243`
- Evidence branch: `snowzlmbot/OpenClaw:proof/issue-101204-live@79f21f82383ac028ef06bea83d47f9091ca0dbd1`
- The fork default branch remains mirror-only and was not modified by this work.
- `Allow edits by maintainers` remains enabled.

## Dependency / contract verification

No dependency, lockfile, package, protocol, or config-schema changes are included. The resolver error code is an internal runtime classification used to preserve the existing fail-closed contract except for the explicitly optional TTS missing-value case.

There is no persisted-data migration: no state schema, serialized runtime format, database, sidecar, or config shape changes. The added resolver tests exercise error classification and provider responses; they do not introduce or migrate stored state.

## Labels considered

Observed automated labels include `gateway`, `docs`, compatibility risk, and security-boundary risk. No contributor-side label mutation was performed. The compatibility/security labels are appropriate because this PR deliberately changes startup behavior for one credential class inside the shared secrets runtime.

## Evidence

Current-head validation:

- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — passed.
- [Focused secrets/startup and live Gateway proof](https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29274584576) — passed on evidence head `79f21f82383ac028ef06bea83d47f9091ca0dbd1` (85 focused tests passed; live Gateway startup/RPC proof passed).
- [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29274563987) — completed on code head `b89582184f0c6612a8187aa00f9416a30faec243`: 38 passed, 11 skipped/neutral, 6 failed, 0 pending. LOC, docs formatting, guards, contracts, security-fast, and the PR's focused behavior gates passed. All six failures are on current-main Control UI model-provider changes: docs map baseline, UI startup request budget, model-provider lint, and one UI dead export; no secrets/TTS file appears in those failure logs.
- [CodeQL](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29274564003) — passed all seven Security High shards on the same code head.
- [OpenGrep PR diff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29274564054) — passed on the same code head.
- [Workflow sanity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29274564205) — passed on the same code head.

## Evidence source map

The downstream proof run above is bound to evidence commit `79f21f82383ac028ef06bea83d47f9091ca0dbd1`, whose parent is the exact PR head `b89582184f0c6612a8187aa00f9416a30faec243`.

It runs the focused resolver/runtime/TTS collector/Discord voice/Gateway startup/TTS handler test set (85 tests passed), then starts a real Gateway with a missing `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` SecretRef and calls `tts.speak`. The uploaded artifact contains both the focused-test log and live-proof log.

## Sanitized logs

Expected proof signals:

```text
[SECRETS_REF_UNAVAILABLE_OPTIONAL] messages.tts.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey ... Environment variable "ELEVENLABS_API_KEY" is missing or empty.
TTS conversion failed: elevenlabs: not configured
PASS: missing optional TTS SecretRef degraded startup and localized TTS failure.
```

Logs use placeholder credential identifiers and contain no credential values.

## Media evidence

This change has no UI or visual state. The behavior is a deterministic startup plus RPC path, so the full GitHub Actions execution and uploaded text logs are the primary evidence; a screenshot or video would not add state that is absent from those logs.

## Risk

- Compatibility: operators who relied on startup fail-fast for an optional TTS key will now discover the absence when TTS is used.
- Security boundary: the exception lives in shared secrets startup code, so the classifier must remain limited to a matching `SECRET_REF_NOT_FOUND` for an assignment explicitly marked optional.
- Regression: independently resolving optional refs adds resolver calls proportional to configured optional TTS refs; the number is bounded by configured TTS provider keys and avoids one missing optional provider masking another valid provider.
- Required credentials, policy denials, invalid refs, provider errors, contract errors, mismatches, and invalid resolved shapes remain fatal and are covered by regression tests.

## Rollback

Revert the single PR commit. No config, database, or data migration rollback is required. Existing SecretRefs remain valid; rollback restores fail-fast startup behavior for missing built-in TTS provider keys.

## Docs updated

- `docs/reference/secretref-credential-surface.md`
- `docs/tools/tts.md`

Both describe the missing-value-only degradation and the normal localized provider-not-configured error.

## Related issue / PR

- Canonical issue: #101204
- Duplicate report: #101205
- Adjacent persona-level SecretRef work: #89607 and #89636 (collection/injection scope, not missing-value startup policy)

## Not tested / limitations

- The live Gateway proof covers a missing env-backed ElevenLabs key.
- Missing file values are covered by optional-runtime tests; missing exec-provider ids are covered by focused resolver classification tests rather than separate live Gateway runs.
- No real provider API call is attempted because the behavior under test is the absent-credential boundary.
- This PR does not add a persistent `degraded` / `configured_unavailable` state or new status/doctor/audit projection. It provides the structured startup warning and localized runtime failure; broader observability remains a separate product-scope decision.
- Maintainer product acceptance is still required for the scoped fail-open startup policy.

## Review context addressed

The refreshed head preserves the reviewed narrow behavior, is rebased on current `main`, and refreshes focused secrets/startup tests plus live Gateway proof on the exact code head. The prior review's stored-data flag is also clarified above: this patch changes no persisted schema or serialized runtime contract.

target.title: fix(node-pairing): require operator.admin to approve fs.listDir nodes (#105936)
target.body:
Closes #105936


## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators with only `operator.pairing` and `operator.write` scopes (without `operator.admin`) could approve a node surface that declares `fs.listDir`, even though invoking `fs.listDir` via `node.invoke` already correctly requires `operator.admin`. This is the same class of approval-versus-invoke scope mismatch previously fixed for `browser.proxy` in #104491.

## Why This Change Was Made

The approval-scope resolver in `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes` determines which operator scopes are required to approve a pending node pairing. It maintains an admin-level command list (`ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`) that dictates which declared commands demand `operator.admin` at approval time. `fs.listDir` was added to the invoke-time admin gate in #105114 but was never included in the approval-time admin list, creating an asymmetry: the approval gate was weaker than the execution gate.

This change adds `NODE_FS_LIST_DIR_COMMAND` to `ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`, making the approval-time scope requirement match the existing invoke-time requirement. The approach is identical to the `browser.proxy` fix in #104491.

## User Impact

Operators with `operator.pairing` and `operator.write` can no longer approve a node pairing that declares `fs.listDir`. Such approvals now require `operator.admin`, consistent with the existing invoke-time authorization. Existing approved pairings are unaffected.

## Evidence

- **Unit test**: `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes(["fs.listDir"])` now returns `["operator.pairing", "operator.admin"]`

```
✓ |unit-fast| src/infra/node-pairing-authz.test.ts (6 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  6 passed (6)
```

- **Integration test**: Full `node.pair.approve` RPC flow via gateway — 12 existing tests continue to pass, confirming no regression to `system.run`, `browser.proxy`, or non-admin command approval paths.

```
✓ |gateway-server| src/gateway/server.node-pairing-authz.test.ts (12 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  12 passed (12)
```

- **Type check**: `tsgo:core` passes without errors.

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: an `operator.write` (non-admin) operator can approve a node advertising the `fs.listDir` capability, whereas invoking `fs.listDir` requires `operator.admin`; the fix makes approval require `operator.admin` too.

Real environment tested: drove the real `approveNodePairing` reducer through its on-disk paired-device store in a fresh temp directory — the real `requestDevicePairing`, `approveDevicePairing`, `requestNodePairing`, `approveNodePairing`, and `resolveMissingRequestedScope` all ran against the real SQLite store, with nothing stubbed (the store was seeded through the real pairing request/approve functions).

Exact steps run after this patch: seed a paired node device, request a node surface declaring `commands: ["fs.listDir"]`, then call `approveNodePairing(requestId, { callerScopes: ["operator.pairing", "operator.write"] }, baseDir)` and record the returned outcome.

Evidence after fix:

```
caller scopes: [operator.pairing, operator.write]
surface commands: [fs.listDir]
approveNodePairing -> FORBIDDEN missingScope=operator.admin

caller scopes: [operator.pairing, operator.admin]
surface commands: [fs.listDir]
approveNodePairing -> APPROVED requestId=0795d316-6191-4d0c-ad8c-a723cb962e00
persisted commands: ["fs.listDir"]
```

## Reviewer Notes

Codex's review notes that the two admin-command classifications
(`ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS` and `ADMIN_ONLY_NODE_INVOKE_COMMANDS`) are
independently maintained, which has now caused two authorization mismatches
(#104491 for `browser.proxy`, this PR for `fs.listDir`).

This concern is well understood. However, the two lists are not identical by
design: `ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS` includes `system.run.*` (which requires
admin at approval time but not at invoke time, since `system.run` is already
protected by agent-layer `BLOCKED_INVOKE_COMMANDS` and descriptor-level scope
alignment), while `ADMIN_ONLY_NODE_INVOKE_COMMANDS` does not. A single shared
constant would either over-approximate one side or lose this semantic
distinction.

For this P1 security fix, I've kept the change minimal — the same pattern that
was merged for `browser.proxy` in #104491. Centralizing the admin-command
classification into a shared policy is a worthwhile follow-up refactor that
deserves more careful design consideration.

---

This PR is AI-assisted. Analysis, implementation, and testing were performed using AI tools (opencode) with review by the author.

target.title: fix(ai): safely format circular rejections in stream catch paths
target.body:
Closes #106570
Related: #106568

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where provider stream failure handling could throw a second exception when formatting a non-Error rejection that contains circular references. That second throw prevented a clean terminal error event and stream end on OpenAI Completions (and the sibling Google shared stream path), so agent runs could hang or fail without a structured provider error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Introduces a shared `formatUnknownError` helper that prefers `Error.message`, safely JSON-stringifies ordinary values, falls back to `String(error)` when `JSON.stringify` throws, and returns the constant `"Unknown error"` if `String()` itself throws (null-prototype or hostile conversion hooks). The OpenAI Completions, Google shared, and Anthropic stream catch paths use it so terminal stream termination cannot be broken by circular or hostile rejection payloads. OpenAI Responses/Azure already guarded stringify; this keeps the unsafe catch sites consistent without new config or fallback policy.

Fix quality: compatibility — no API/config shape change, same errorMessage field; performance — O(1) catch-path only; usability — still delivers a terminal error message; security — no secret logging or trust-boundary changes.

## User Impact

When a provider transport rejects with an unusual non-Error object (including circular structures or values whose String conversion throws), the agent stream fails closed with a normal error stop reason and message instead of throwing inside the recovery path.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Node v24.17.0)

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/utils/format-unknown-error.test.ts
# 4 passed (Error.message, JSON path, circular String fallback, non-throwing final literal)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts \
  packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.test.ts \
  -t "circular"
# 2 passed (OpenAI #106570 + Google #106568 lifecycle: stopReason=error + non-empty errorMessage)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts -t "circular" --reporter=verbose
# ✓ emits a terminal error for circular non-Error rejections without rethrowing (#106570)

pnpm exec oxfmt --check packages/ai/src/utils/format-unknown-error.ts \
  packages/ai/src/utils/format-unknown-error.test.ts  # pass
git diff --check  # pass
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Stream catch paths must emit a terminal error event when the transport rejects with a circular non-Error value (or a value whose String conversion throws), without a second exception in the recovery path.
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout; focused Vitest via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`; Node v24.17.0 runtime transcript for the formatter + stream-shaped terminal events. No live provider credentials required (SDK circular non-Error shapes are not guaranteed from supported providers; proof exercises the catch-path contract the providers call).
- Current-main contrast: On main, `error instanceof Error ? error.message : JSON.stringify(error)` throws `TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON` for self-referential objects, so the catch path never reaches `stream.push({ type: "error" })` / `stream.end()`. Reproduced with: `const c={k:1}; c.self=c; JSON.stringify(c)` → throws.
- Exact steps after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/utils/format-unknown-error.test.ts`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts -t "circular"`
  3. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.test.ts -t "circular"`
  4. Runtime transcript (formatter + stream-shaped terminal emission; redacted, no secrets):
```text
=== formatUnknownError runtime proof (redacted) ===
host: darwin v24.17.0
before: JSON.stringify(circular) throws: true
format(circular): threw=false value="[object Object]"
format(null-proto-circular): threw=false value="Unknown error"
format(hostile-circular): threw=false value="Unknown error"
format(Error): threw=false value="upstream boom"
format(plain-object): threw=false value="{\"code\":\"ECONNRESET\"}"

=== stream catch-path terminal emission (synthetic runtime, OpenAI Completions shape) ===
case=circular-non-Error
  output.stopReason= error
  output.errorMessage= [object Object]
  events= [{"type":"error","reason":"error","errorMessage":"[object Object]"},{"type":"end"}]
  stream_closed= true
case=null-proto-circular
  output.stopReason= error
  output.errorMessage= Unknown error
  events= [{"type":"error","reason":"error","errorMessage":"Unknown error"},{"type":"end"}]
  stream_closed= true
case=hostile-circular
  output.stopReason= error
  output.errorMessage= Unknown error
  events= [{"type":"error","reason":"error","errorMessage":"Unknown error"},{"type":"end"}]
  stream_closed= true
proof_ok=true
```
- Evidence after fix: Focused OpenAI/Google lifecycle cases pass with `stopReason === "error"` and a non-empty `errorMessage`. Helper never throws: circular → `[object Object]`; null-prototype/hostile circular → `"Unknown error"`. Runtime events show `{type:"error"}` then stream end for each case.
- Control check: Ordinary Error rejections still use `error.message`; ordinary plain objects still JSON-stringify; only circular non-Errors take the String fallback; only values that break both JSON and String take the constant literal.
- Observed result after fix: Circular and hostile non-Error rejections produce a terminal stream error instead of a secondary serialization/conversion crash.
- What was not tested: Live OpenAI/Google network failures that happen to reject with circular non-Error SDK payloads; Anthropic live path (same helper wired for sibling invariant only).

---

## Summary

- Preserves local package overrides during package update flows, including standalone added `dist` files, and reports the recovery bundle when overrides are not reapplied.
- Keeps content-inventory validation strict for new tarballs while allowing already-published `2026.6.5` / `2026.6.5-beta.6` packages that predate `dist/postinstall-content-inventory.json`.
- Repairs the `main` merge conflict on `src/cli/update-cli.ts` and `src/infra/update-runner.ts`, then refreshes the branch to current `upstream/main`.
- Adds the missing zh-CN glossary entries needed for the docs check after the latest main merge.

## Verification

- `pnpm docs:list`
- `PATH=/Users/jason/.nvm/versions/node/v24.14.0/bin:$PATH pnpm check:docs`
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD && git diff --check`

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Package self-update preserves local packaged `dist` overrides, captures edits through the staged swap boundary, fails closed on unsafe replay topology and package metadata, and verifies content hashes plus executable semantics.

Real environment tested: Local macOS source checkout on current PR head `4451b9f3fedf5ea1e327101c768509bb9178d8e1`, Node `v24.14.0`, plus fresh Linux Blacksmith Testbox runs. target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false vitest run --project extension-codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` passed (149 tests)
- focused Slack replies + identity-fallback tests passed (85 tests)
- `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` passed (10 tests)
- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false tsgo:extensions` passed
- formatter check on touched files passed
- `git diff --check` passed

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`
- generic tool progress kind: `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND = "tool-progress"`
- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`
- existing fast-mode kind remains: `FAST_MODE_AUTO_PROGRESS_KIND = "fast-mode-auto"`

Codex no longer exports Codex-named public progress symbols. Codex marks only transient automatic tool summaries with the generic `tool-progress` kind; completed/failed/verbose terminal output is left unmarked and remains deliverable. Callable public SDK budget was raised with the additive predicate.

## Live Slack Proof
Generated against the TCG Slack API from PR branch code on 2026-07-11 02:18 UTC at exact head `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`. Channel is redacted; it was the Jack bot App Home/DM proof surface, not a client or public channel.

      }
    }
  },
  "noThreadProgressChrome": {
    "input": "✍️ Write: MEMORY.md",
    "call": "sendMessageSlack(..., { progressChrome: true, progressChromeReaction: writing_hand }) from PR branch head",
    "result": {

  "completedToolOutput": {

      "text": "Slack progress-chrome exact-head lifecycle proof anchor 2026-07-11T02:18:21.368Z head=1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5",
      "reactions": ["hammer_and_wrench"]
    },

## Verification
- Thread-scoped typed progress chrome converts to a reaction/suppressed result instead of `chat.postMessage`.
- Progress chrome without a reaction target is suppressed before Slack post.
- Completed tool output without progress metadata remains sendable.
- Failed tool output without progress metadata remains sendable.
- Explicit verbose output without progress metadata remains sendable.
- Semantic replies using the same leading emoji and embedded command remain sendable.

target.title: fix(skills): globally-installed ClawHub skills falsely show as not tracked [AI-assisted]
target.body:
> [AI-assisted] This PR was generated using Claude Code.

Closes #105530

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who install a ClawHub skill **globally** (`openclaw skills install <slug> --global`, living under the managed dir `~/.openclaw/skills/<slug>` and tracked in the **global** lockfile `~/.openclaw/.clawhub/lock.json`) would see the skill falsely reported as `ClawHub link invalid` in `openclaw skills status` and the Control UI, with the message:

> Skill `<slug>` has ClawHub origin metadata but is not tracked by the workspace ClawHub lockfile.

The skill is in fact correctly installed and tracked - just in the global lockfile, not the workspace one.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` read the ClawHub lockfile exclusively from the workspace directory (`readClawHubSkillsLockfileStatusSync(workspaceDir)`) and passed that single read to `resolveClawHubSkillStatusLinkSync` for every non-bundled skill. For a globally-installed skill (`source: "openclaw-managed"`), the tracking entry lives in the **managed** lockfile at `<dirname(managedSkillsDir)>/.clawhub/lock.json`, so the workspace lookup misses it and returns `invalid`.

The fix resolves the link status for `openclaw-managed` skills against the managed lockfile (and the managed parent dir, so the expected-install-dir check matches the skill dir) instead of the workspace lockfile. Workspace-local skills are unchanged. Detection uses the loader-assigned `source` rather than a lexical path check, because managed skill roots may contain symlinks whose resolved `baseDir` sits outside the `managedSkillsDir` tree.

## User Impact

Globally installed ClawHub skills now show as correctly `linked` in `openclaw skills status` and the Control UI skills view, instead of a false `ClawHub link invalid` / "not tracked" warning. Workspace-local skill status is unaffected.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof captured on Windows 10 by running the production `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` against real on-disk lockfiles (standalone `tsx` repro script run locally; before/after output below). The script creates a managed (global) install - skill dir under `managedSkillsDir` with `.clawhub/origin.json`, plus a global lockfile at `<managedParent>/.clawhub/lock.json` tracking it - and a separate workspace whose own lockfile does **not** track the skill.

BEFORE (unpatched main) - the globally-installed skill is falsely `invalid`, read against the **workspace** lockfile:

```
"skillSource": "openclaw-managed",
"clawhub": {
  "status": "invalid",
  "valid": false,
  "reason": "Skill \"agentreceipt\" has ClawHub origin metadata but is not tracked by the workspace ClawHub lockfile.",
  "slug": "agentreceipt",
  "lockPath": "...\\openclaw-workspace-fYctHw\\.clawhub\\lock.json"
}
```

AFTER (this patch) - the same skill is correctly `linked`, read against the **managed (global)** lockfile:

```
"skillSource": "openclaw-managed",
"clawhub": {
  "status": "linked",
  "valid": true,
  "registry": "https://clawhub.ai",
  "slug": "agentreceipt",
  "installedVersion": "1.2.3",
  "lockPath": "...\\openclaw-managed-83CHpB\\.clawhub\\lock.json"
}
```

Regression tests added in `src/skills/discovery/status.test.ts`:
- links a globally-installed skill via the managed lockfile (asserts `status: "linked"`)
- reports a globally-installed skill as `invalid` when it is absent from the managed lockfile (guards against falsely linking)

Full skill-status suite passes (`pnpm test -- src/skills/discovery/status.test.ts` -> 13 passed, 1 skipped on win32).

## Real Behavior Proof

- Behavior addressed: Globally installed ClawHub skills (`source: "openclaw-managed"`) are falsely reported as `invalid` / "not tracked by the workspace ClawHub lockfile" because `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` only consults the workspace lockfile.
- Real environment tested: Windows 10, Node v22.22.3, OpenClaw main @ 50e5ffcd25, running the production `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` function from `src/skills/discovery/status.ts` via `pnpm exec tsx`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: a standalone `tsx` script builds a managed/global install (skill dir + `.clawhub/origin.json` + global lockfile tracking the slug) and a separate workspace whose lockfile omits the slug, then calls `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus(workspaceDir, { managedSkillsDir, entries })` and prints the resolved `clawhub` status.
- Evidence after fix:
```
AFTER (patched):
"clawhub": { "status": "linked", "valid": true, "slug": "agentreceipt",
  "lockPath": "...\\openclaw-managed-83CHpB\\.clawhub\\lock.json" }

BEFORE (unpatched main):
"clawhub": { "status": "invalid", "valid": false,
  "reason": "Skill \"agentreceipt\" has ClawHub origin metadata but is not tracked by the workspace ClawHub lockfile.",
  "lockPath": "...\\openclaw-workspace-fYctHw\\.clawhub\\lock.json" }
```
- Observed result after fix: The globally-installed skill resolves to `status: "linked"` against the managed (global) lockfile instead of `invalid` against the workspace lockfile. The `lockPath` in the resolved status now points at the global lockfile.
- What was not tested: End-to-end through a running gateway / live Control UI render; the real `openclaw skills status` CLI against a real `~/.openclaw` home. The proof exercises the real production status function with real on-disk lockfiles, which is the exact code path the CLI and UI consume.

## Human Verification

Verified: the production `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` code path with real on-disk managed + workspace lockfiles (before/after), scoped `pnpm test` for the skills status suite, `pnpm tsgo` (type check), `pnpm format:check`, scoped `oxlint --type-aware` on the changed files. Not verified: Swift (skipped on Windows), full `pnpm test` suite, live Control UI rendering. Note: local `pnpm build` (tsdown) hit a V8 out-of-memory crash on this Windows machine (a known low-memory local-env quirk, unrelated to this 3-line logic change); relying on CI's build check on a properly-sized runner.

## Security Impact

- Does this change authentication, authorization, or trust boundaries? No.
- Does this change credential, secret, or token handling? No.
- Does this change sandboxing or process isolation? No.
- Does this change network boundaries or external API calls? No.
- Does this introduce a new trust boundary or change an existing one? No.

No CODEOWNERS secops paths are touched (`src/skills/` is not secops-owned). The change only affects which local lockfile is consulted for a status display.

## Compatibility / Migration

No config, API, CLI, or lockfile-format changes. The set of inputs/outputs of `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` is unchanged; only the accuracy of the `clawhub` status for globally-installed skills improves. No migration required.

## Failure Recovery

If the managed lockfile read regresses, globally-installed skills would revert to the prior `invalid` / "not tracked" display behavior - a cosmetic status misreport, not a crash or data loss. The change is read-only with respect to lockfiles (no writes), so there is no risk of lockfile corruption. Reverting the commit fully restores prior behavior.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Risk**: A skill whose loader-assigned `source` is `openclaw-managed` but whose lockfile entry legitimately lives in the workspace lockfile would now be looked up in the managed lockfile. **Mitigation**: managed skills are, by definition, installed under `managedSkillsDir` and tracked in the managed lockfile; workspace-local skills use other `source` values and are unaffected. Added a regression test for the "absent from managed lockfile" case to ensure such a skill still reports `invalid` rather than falsely `linked`.
- **Risk**: Competing/sibling PR on the same issue. **Mitigation**: this PR supplies the real-behavior-proof (real production-function output with real on-disk lockfiles, before/after) that the issue's proof gate requires, rather than a screenshot.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I will respond to review comments in the review conversation where they were left.
- [x] I understand review conversations belong to the reviewer and I should not resolve them myself unless requested.

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).
